target.title: fix(mcp-grant): guard sessionKey.trim() against undefined input
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`mintAttachGrant` calls `params.sessionKey.trim()` assuming a string, but the caller resolves it via `readString() ?? resolveMainSessionKey()`. If both return `undefined`, `.trim()` throws `TypeError` instead of reaching the validation guard.

## Why This Change Was Made

`params.sessionKey?.trim() ?? ""` — undefined flows through to `if (!sessionKey)` check instead of crashing.

## User Impact

Prevents TypeError crash when MCP attach grants are requested without a valid session key.

## Evidence

![runtime proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhangLei99586/openclaw/proof-screenshots/pr-99488-99490-proof.png)

- OLD: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim')`
- NEW: gracefully reaches validation guard "sessionKey is required"

target.title: fix: chat.send no reply when thinking metadata is set
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a normal `chat.send` message with per-message `thinking` metadata could persist the user turn but produce no assistant response. The gateway was converting structured `thinking` metadata into textual `/think ...` command input, so clients without text slash-command authority could have a normal message treated as command text before model dispatch.

No related open GitHub issue or PR was found. I searched live GitHub and local gitcrawl for `chat.send thinking`, Android/chat no-reply reports, `/think` command-body reports, and paired-device slash-command authorization reports. The only direct keyword hit was already-merged #79385, which is a broader thinking/fast controls PR rather than this no-reply bug report.

## Why This Change Was Made

`chat.send` already has a structured dispatch path for one-turn thinking metadata via `replyOptions.thinkingLevelOverride`. This PR removes the duplicate `/think <level> <message>` rewrite for normal messages, leaving `CommandBody`, `BodyForCommands`, and `CommandTurn.body` as the user’s actual message while still passing the requested thinking override to reply resolution.

The review pass also hardened the adjacent reply/model-selection behavior so explicit thinking-off inputs, per-agent thinking defaults, and per-model `params.thinking` defaults prevent model reasoning defaults from being re-enabled during normal directive resolution and auto-fallback primary probes.

## User Impact

Mobile, WebChat, consult, and other `chat.send` clients can set a one-shot thinking level without accidentally turning a normal user message into a text slash command. `thinking` remains turn-local metadata: it applies to the dispatched run, does not alter the visible/user command text, and does not persist `thinkingLevel` into the session store.

## Evidence

Behavioral proof:

- `chat.send` with `message: "hello from phone"` and `thinking: "low"` now dispatches with `BodyForCommands === "hello from phone"`, `CommandBody === "hello from phone"`, `CommandTurn.kind === "normal"`, and `replyOptions.thinkingLevelOverride === "low"`.
- The persisted session store is checked at the canonical `agent:main:main` key and the legacy `main` view to prove one-turn `thinking` metadata does not become durable session `thinkingLevel`.
- Auto-fallback tests cover `params.thinking` values `false`, `"disabled"`, and `"none"` so configured thinking-off aliases keep reasoning defaults off when probing a primary model.

Validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/chat.directive-tags.test.ts -t "chat.send keeps thinking metadata out of command text for normal messages"` - passed, 2 tests run with unrelated tests skipped.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat.test.ts -t "chat.send does not persist one-turn thinking metadata"` - passed, 1 test run with unrelated tests skipped.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.auto-fallback.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-directives.target-session.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts` - passed, 173 tests.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo` - passed.
- `corepack pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 <10 touched TS files>` - passed.
- `git diff --check 7fa26e088d283f9dbde607d1148e62c682b7d471 && git diff --check` - passed.
- A broad affected-file Vitest run hit older media/inline-reply failures in `chat.directive-tags.test.ts`; the new thinking test and a representative media failure case both passed in isolation, so this is recorded as a validation caveat rather than an accepted regression from this PR.

Review proof:

- Native Codex review: 3 consecutive clean whole-target passes after review fixes.
- Independent cold review: 3 consecutive clean reviewer passes on the same final tree.

AI-assisted: yes. A sanitized transcript was not included because adding transcript logs requires explicit approval.

target.title: fix #99163: harden large chat attachment parsing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large clipboard image data URLs currently pass through whole-string base64 validation and full-payload MIME sniffing. For multi-megabyte attachments this does unnecessary work on the hot path and can make attachment parsing much more expensive than the small header sniff actually needs.

## Summary

- replace chat attachment base64 validation regex with an iterative scanner so large clipboard payloads avoid whole-string regexp matching
- move the stack-safe large-payload fix into `canonicalizeBase64`, preserving full malformed-tail validation for shared callers
- make MIME sniffing decode only a small canonical base64 prefix after full payload validation
- add regression coverage for ~1.9MB PNG clipboard data URLs, large shared canonicalization, and malformed data after a valid PNG prefix

Fixes #99163.

## Evidence

Real Gateway parser proof using a generated valid PNG data URL on this PR head:

```json
{
  "proof": "gateway chat.send attachment parser large PNG data URL",
  "pngBytes": 1901669,

}
```

Validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/media-core/src/base64.test.ts src/media/sniff-mime-from-base64.test.ts src/gateway/chat-attachments.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — 127 passed across media-core, media sniffing, and gateway shards
- `OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs packages/media-core/src/base64.ts packages/media-core/src/base64.test.ts src/media/sniff-mime-from-base64.ts src/media/sniff-mime-from-base64.test.ts src/gateway/chat-attachments.ts src/gateway/chat-attachments.test.ts` — passed
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.non-agents.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test-non-agents.tsbuildinfo` — passed
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 packages/media-core/src/base64.ts packages/media-core/src/base64.test.ts src/media/sniff-mime-from-base64.ts src/media/sniff-mime-from-base64.test.ts src/gateway/chat-attachments.ts src/gateway/chat-attachments.test.ts` — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed

Note: this revision preserves the shared `sniffMimeFromBase64` full-input validation contract that ClawSweeper flagged. A valid PNG prefix with an invalid base64 tail now returns `undefined`, while large valid payloads still sniff from a bounded decoded prefix and avoid full-payload `Buffer.from(..., "base64")` on the gateway path.

target.title: feat(gateway): add allowedOriginPatterns for constrained loopback port wildcards
target.body:
Closes #98383

## What Problem This Solves

Remote WebView-hosted node clients (e.g. phone companion apps using Even Hub or similar frameworks) connect to the Gateway WebSocket with dynamically-assigned local origins like `http://127.0.0.1:<random-port>`. The current `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` only supports exact origins or the global `["*"]` wildcard, forcing users to choose between two inadequate options:

- **Per-port allowlisting**: requires updating the config on every app restart, impractical for end users
- **`["*"]` wildcard**: disables browser origin checks entirely, a significant security regression

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `gateway.controlUi.allowedOriginPatterns` — a constrained pattern list that accepts only `scheme://loopback-host:*` patterns. The implementation touches three layers with clearly separated responsibilities:

**1. Zod schema (config load time — fail-close)**

Each pattern must pass six checks: valid format (`scheme://host:*`), explicit protocol (`http:` or `https:`), port-level `*` wildcard only, no host wildcards, and hostname in the loopback literal set (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `[::1]`). Illegal patterns prevent service startup — no silent downgrades.

**2. Runtime matching (`checkBrowserOrigin`)**

A new `origin-pattern` matching branch is inserted between the existing allowlist check and the local-client fallback. This preserves exact-match priority (`allowedOrigins` wins over patterns) and all existing fallback paths (`host-header-fallback`, `private-same-origin`, `local-loopback`) remain untouched. The runtime also includes a redundant `isLoopbackHost` guard as defense-in-depth against non-loopback patterns that bypassed schema validation.

**3. Startup config validation**

- `server-runtime-config.ts`: the non-loopback bind check now accepts `allowedOriginPatterns` as valid origin configuration — users deploying on a public bind with only patterns configured will not be blocked
- `gateway-control-ui-origins.ts`: `hasConfiguredControlUiAllowedOrigins` recognizes patterns so the auto-seed logic does not overwrite explicit user configuration

**4. Codex review follow-up**

- `schema.help.ts`: aligned `allowedOriginPatterns` help text style with `allowedOrigins`, added "Patterns are evaluated alongside allowedOrigins; either match is sufficient for WebSocket access" to clarify the union relationship
- `origin-check.test.ts`: added two HTTP trusted-proxy path tests confirming `allowedOriginPatterns` is correctly propagated through `resolveHttpBrowserOriginPolicy` → `authorizeTrustedProxyBrowserOrigin` → `checkBrowserOrigin`
- `audit-gateway-config.ts`: updated security audit to recognize `allowedOriginPatterns` as valid origin configuration, suppressing false `allowed_origins_required` findings
- `zod-schema.ts`: added `.describe()` metadata for `allowedOriginPatterns`
- `schema.help.ts`: updated `allowedOrigins` help text to reference `allowedOriginPatterns` as a safer alternative for dynamic loopback port clients
- `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md` and `docs/gateway/troubleshooting.md`: added `allowedOriginPatterns` to public docs and origin-error remediation guidance

**Design constraints preserved across the stack:**

- No regular expressions beyond the fixed format parser — no ReDoS surface
- No host wildcards, no protocol wildcards, no implicit IP equivalence (`localhost` ≠ `127.0.0.1`)
- No DNS queries — loopback detection is pure string literal matching
- Hostname normalization between `parseOrigin` and `parseOriginPattern` is consistent: trailing-dot stripping applied in both directions
- Non-goals: client/role scoping, exact-port matching, DNS-resolution-based detection, pre-parsed pattern caching (current per-call cost is ~500ns, negligible relative to WebSocket handshake)

## User Impact

Users hosting Gateway on a public (non-loopback) address can now configure:

```json
{
  "gateway": {
    "controlUi": {
      "allowedOriginPatterns": ["http://127.0.0.1:*"]
    }
  }
}
```

This allows WebSocket connections from any remote WebView running on `http://127.0.0.1:<any-port>` without resorting to `["*"]`. The full loopback family is supported (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `[::1]`, both `http:` and `https:` protocols).

**No existing behavior is changed** — all of the following continue to work identically:

- `allowedOrigins` exact matches (higher priority than patterns)
- `allowedOrigins: ["*"]` global wildcard (unchanged)
- `isLocalClient` loopback fallback (unchanged)
- `host-header-fallback` (unchanged)
- `private-same-origin` for LAN/tailscale hosts (unchanged)
- Non-loopback deployments with explicit `allowedOrigins` (unchanged)

Users currently on `["*"]` for WebView support can migrate to `["http://127.0.0.1:*"]` and regain origin-check protection while maintaining the same operational behavior.

**Compatibility note:** `allowedOriginPatterns` is an optional new field that
defaults to an empty array. Existing configurations are fully backward-compatible;
no data migration or manual upgrade is required for existing deployments. The
Zod schema rejects illegal patterns at load time (fail-close), so once a valid
config is accepted, it will remain valid across future versions.

## Evidence

**Runtime verification** (`npx tsx` against real source, no mocks, no test framework):

```
30/30 tests passed

─── A: Zod Schema allowedOriginPatterns (11/11) ───
  ✅ A1: http://127.0.0.1:* accepted
  ✅ A2: http://localhost:* accepted
  ✅ A3: http://[::1]:* accepted
  ✅ A4: https://127.0.0.1:* accepted
  ✅ A5: non-loopback hostname rejected
  ✅ A6: exact port without * rejected
  ✅ A7: host wildcard http://*:* rejected
  ✅ A8: bare * rejected
  ✅ A9: ftp protocol rejected
  ✅ A10: empty patterns array accepted (no regression)
  ✅ A11: allowedOrigins + allowedOriginPatterns coexist

─── B: checkBrowserOrigin runtime matching (15/15) ───
  ✅ B1: http://127.0.0.1:40313 matches pattern [CORE ISSUE SCENARIO]
  ✅ B2: http://localhost:5173 matches http://localhost:*

  ✅ B5: http://127.0.0.1 (no explicit port) matches pattern

  ✅ B8: protocol mismatch rejected

```

target.title: fix(anthropic): wire buildGuardedModelFetch into the Cloudflare createClient branch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Anthropic provider (`anthropic.ts`) creates five `Anthropic` SDK clients — one for Cloudflare AI Gateway, one for GitHub Copilot, one for Microsoft Foundry bearer auth, one for OAuth, and one for the API-key fallback. None of them passed a custom `fetch` option. Streaming Anthropic calls from these providers bypassed the guarded provider transport — SSRF protection, request timeout, retry-hint injection, and response lifecycle management that every other Anthropic SDK path already has.

This PR injects `fetch: buildGuardedModelFetch(model)` into the **Cloudflare AI Gateway** SDK constructor specifically, bringing that branch to guarded-fetch parity with:
- `anthropic-transport-stream.ts:788` (managed Anthropic transport)
- `openai-responses.ts` (#97848)
- `openai-completions.ts` (#97228)
- `azure-openai-responses.ts`

  - Microsoft Foundry bearer (#98015)

This is **one of five split PRs** that supersede #97868.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildGuardedModelFetch` is the canonical fetch wrapper applied to every Anthropic SDK constructor in the codebase. The Anthropic SDK accepts `fetch?: Fetch` per its constructor options. The Cloudflare branch was missing this wrapper.

The change is 2 lines in production code (`+1 import, +1 fetch:` option). The proof is focused on showing the guard is actually in scope and active:
- A mocked constructor assertion in `anthropic.test.ts`.
- An SSRF-block test that stubs `globalThis.fetch` and proves the guard intercepts a private IP before the SDK reaches the default fetch.

## Evidence

  src/llm/providers/anthropic.test.ts \

### Layer 2: SSRF-block guard-specific proof

`anthropic-cloudflare.fetch-proof.test.ts` stubs `globalThis.fetch` as a call counter, configures `baseUrl: http://169.254.169.254/v1`, and asserts `globalFetchCalled === 0`. This proves `buildGuardedModelFetch` intercepts the blocked target before the SDK falls back to `globalThis.fetch`.

### Maintainer-hosted smoke

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `createClient` in `src/llm/providers/anthropic.ts` (Cloudflare branch) now passes `fetch: buildGuardedModelFetch(model)` to `new Anthropic({...})`, so Anthropic calls routed through the Cloudflare AI Gateway inherit OpenClaw guarded-fetch policy.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v22.22.0, local source checkout.
- **Exact steps**: see Evidence above.
- **Evidence after fix**: 37/37 tests pass. Layer 1 proves the wrapper is wired; Layer 2 proves the guard actively blocks private-IP targets.
- **Observed result after fix**: the Cloudflare Anthropic constructor now carries a custom `fetch`, and the guard rejects `169.254.169.254` before any network call.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can already move from a selected/default model route to a fallback model route or rotate auth profiles when a primary profile fails, but there was no optional runtime hook for operators to send a sanitized fallback-enter, fallback-cleared, or auth-profile-fallback event to their own alerting surface. This adds a disabled-by-default reporter that only sends when an endpoint and token are configured. It emits model fallback enter/clear and auth-profile fallback transitions, sanitizes bounded fields, supports token-file based configuration, surfaces non-2xx ingest failures, and suppresses duplicate direct model fallback alerts when the auto-reply path can emit the resolved active route.

target.title: feat(signal): show status reactions during inbound replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal users could receive a normal agent reply without the lifecycle status reactions already available in other message channels. When status reactions are configured, Signal can now show that an inbound message was acknowledged, is being processed, is using tools or compacting, has stalled, and then completed or failed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal inbound handling now uses the shared status-reaction controller behind the existing `messages.statusReactions.enabled`, acknowledgement scope, and Signal `reactionLevel` gates. Direct messages react to the inbound sender/timestamp; group messages react through the group id plus the original message author; reaction send/remove failures are logged without blocking the agent dispatch path.

The shared dispatch path also forwards opted-in compaction lifecycle callbacks when normal progress text is hidden, so reaction-only progress can still move through compacting and back to thinking.

The observed `⏳` hourglass is intentional. It is the shared soft-stall status (`stallSoft`) from the default status-reaction timing, and Signal also uses it as the default hard-stall reaction so a long-running turn does not look like a terminal failure. Explicit configured `messages.statusReactions.emojis.stallHard` overrides are still honored.

## User Impact

Configured Signal routes can show live status reactions during an agent turn instead of only typing/read feedback. Replies that are sent through message tools are treated as successful visible replies, so the final status does not incorrectly flash as an error when the reply was delivered through that path.

## Evidence

Manual Signal proof:

target.title: fix(config): skip .openclaw append when OPENCLAW_HOME already names a state dir (#45765)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Setting `OPENCLAW_HOME` directly to an existing state directory such as `.openclaw` or `.clawdbot` could produce nested paths like `.openclaw/.openclaw`, while malformed sentinel values like `"undefined"` / `"null"` needed to remain treated as unset to match home-dir normalization.

## Evidence
Fresh focused proof from this maintenance cycle: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/paths.test.ts src/utils.test.ts` passed; `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 "src/config/state-dir-names.ts" "src/config/paths.ts" "src/config/paths.test.ts" "src/utils.ts" "src/utils.test.ts"` passed; `pnpm tsgo` passed with only the repo Node engine warning; `git diff --check` passed; LSP diagnostics were clean for all touched config/path files.

---

## Summary

Setting `OPENCLAW_HOME=~/.openclaw` produces the nested directory `~/.openclaw/.openclaw/` and onboarding writes the config file to the wrong place. Reporter on Linux Kylin V10 / aarch64 (and macOS 15.4) documented a 100% reproduction rate on OpenClaw 2026.3.12 (#45765). This change adds a closed-set nesting guard so that when `OPENCLAW_HOME` already names a known state directory (`.openclaw` or the legacy `.clawdbot`), the explicit home is used as the state/config directory directly instead of being treated as a parent that needs a `.openclaw` subdirectory.

## Root Cause

- `src/config/paths.ts:60-89` — `resolveStateDir()` calls `newStateDir(effectiveHomedir)` which unconditionally appends `NEW_STATE_DIRNAME = ".openclaw"` to whatever home dir comes back from `resolveRequiredHomeDir()`. When the operator explicitly set `OPENCLAW_HOME=~/.openclaw`, the resolved home is already `~/.openclaw`, so the helper produces `~/.openclaw/.openclaw`.
- `src/utils.ts:119-141` — `resolveConfigDir()` does the same: `path.join(resolveRequiredHomeDir(env, homedir), ".openclaw")`.
- `src/config/paths.ts:272-296` — `resolveDefaultConfigCandidates()` builds candidate config paths through the same `newStateDir(effectiveHomedir)` / `legacyStateDirs(effectiveHomedir)` helpers and emits the nested `~/.openclaw/.openclaw/openclaw.json` path as the canonical first candidate. Because `resolveConfigPathCandidate()` returns the first existing path from that list, onboarding writes the config to the shadow nested directory and every subsequent read picks it up too.
- Execution path: `openclaw onboard` → `resolveConfigPathCandidate` → `resolveDefaultConfigCandidates` → `newStateDir(effectiveHomedir)` → `path.join(~/.openclaw, ".openclaw")` → writes config to `~/.openclaw/.openclaw/openclaw.json`.

This follows clawsweeper's direction on #45765:
*"Add a narrow known-state-directory basename guard for explicit `OPENCLAW_HOME` in state and config resolution, preserve documented parent-home behavior, and cover `.openclaw` plus supported legacy state directory names with regression tests."*

## Changes

- `src/config/paths.ts`:
  - Export `ALL_STATE_DIRNAMES` (`ReadonlySet<string>`) combining `NEW_STATE_DIRNAME` (`.openclaw`) and `LEGACY_STATE_DIRNAMES` (`.clawdbot`). Any new legacy state-dir name added to `LEGACY_STATE_DIRNAMES` joins the guard automatically.
  - Export `isExplicitOpenClawHomeStateDir(env, resolvedHome)` — returns `true` only when `env.OPENCLAW_HOME?.trim()` is non-empty AND `path.basename(resolvedHome)` is in `ALL_STATE_DIRNAMES`. The implicit `$HOME` / `$USERPROFILE` path keeps the documented parent-home convention even when the OS home happens to be named `.openclaw`; we opt in only when the operator was explicit.
  - `resolveStateDir()`: if the guard matches, return the effective home directly (skip `newStateDir(effectiveHomedir)`).
  - `resolveDefaultConfigCandidates()`: if the guard matches, use `[home]` as the single default directory list instead of `[newStateDir, ...legacyStateDirs]`, so candidate paths become `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` (and the legacy filename variants under the same dir) instead of `~/.openclaw/.openclaw/openclaw.json`.
- `src/utils.ts`:
  - Import `isExplicitOpenClawHomeStateDir` from `./config/paths.js` (no circular dependency — `paths.ts` does not import from `utils.ts`).
  - `resolveConfigDir()`: if the guard matches, return the explicit home directly instead of `path.join(home, ".openclaw")`.
- `src/config/paths.test.ts`: add 6 new regression cases under a new `OPENCLAW_HOME nesting guard (#45765)` describe block covering: `ALL_STATE_DIRNAMES` membership; `isExplicitOpenClawHomeStateDir` true/false matrix; `resolveStateDir` + `resolveDefaultConfigCandidates` for `.openclaw` and `.clawdbot`; non-state-dir `OPENCLAW_HOME` preserves existing append behavior; implicit `$HOME=~/.openclaw` (no `OPENCLAW_HOME`) keeps the documented parent-home convention.
- `src/utils.test.ts`: add 3 new regression cases covering `resolveConfigDir` for `.openclaw`, `.clawdbot`, and the non-state-dir `OPENCLAW_HOME` regression check.

## Reproduction (before fix)

Source-reproducible against current `upstream/main` (`12e5876903`):

~~~text
$ node --import tsx ./smoke-before-fix.mjs
OPENCLAW_HOME=/home/user/.openclaw
  resolveStateDir   -> /home/user/.openclaw/.openclaw   (BUG: nested)
  resolveConfigDir  -> /home/user/.openclaw/.openclaw   (BUG: nested)
  candidates[0]     -> /home/user/.openclaw/.openclaw/openclaw.json   (BUG: writes shadow file)
~~~

## Verification (after fix)

~~~text
$ node --import tsx ./smoke-45765.mjs
PASS: OPENCLAW_HOME=/home/user/.openclaw (#45765 case)
  resolveStateDir       -> /home/user/.openclaw           (fixed; no nesting)
  resolveConfigDir      -> /home/user/.openclaw           (fixed; no nesting)
  candidates[0]         -> /home/user/.openclaw/openclaw.json   (writes the canonical path)
  no nested .openclaw   OK
PASS: OPENCLAW_HOME=/home/user/.clawdbot (legacy)
  resolveStateDir       -> /home/user/.clawdbot
  resolveConfigDir      -> /home/user/.clawdbot
  candidates[0]         -> /home/user/.clawdbot/openclaw.json
  no nested .openclaw   OK
PASS: OPENCLAW_HOME=/srv/openclaw-home (non-state-dir; existing behavior must remain)
  resolveStateDir       -> /srv/openclaw-home/.openclaw   (unchanged; parent-home convention preserved)
  resolveConfigDir      -> /srv/openclaw-home/.openclaw
  candidates[0]         -> /srv/openclaw-home/.openclaw/openclaw.json
  no nested .openclaw   OK

RESULTS: 3 pass / 0 fail / 3 total
~~~

## Test

- `pnpm test src/config/paths.test.ts` — 29 passed (incl. 6 new `OPENCLAW_HOME nesting guard` regression cases)
- `pnpm test src/utils.test.ts` — 18 passed (incl. 3 new `OPENCLAW_HOME nesting guard` regression cases)
- `pnpm test src/infra/home-dir.test.ts` — 27 passed (no regressions in the underlying home-dir resolver)
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed (production typecheck clean)

## Notes

- Scope: 4 files, +140/-2 LOC. Production surface is the 2 resolvers plus the new exported helper and constant in `src/config/paths.ts`; the rest is the expanded regression test coverage.
- Compatibility: preserved across all existing entry points.
  - `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` explicit overrides take priority before the guard (existing `resolveStateDir` / `resolveConfigDir` early returns are unchanged).
  - `OPENCLAW_HOME=/srv/openclaw-home` and any other non-state-dir basename still resolves to `/srv/openclaw-home/.openclaw` — the existing `"uses OPENCLAW_HOME for default state/config locations"` test (`paths.test.ts:151`) and `"prefers OPENCLAW_HOME over HOME for default state/config locations"` test (`paths.test.ts:158`) continue to pass without modification.
  - Implicit `$HOME=~/.openclaw` (no `OPENCLAW_HOME` set) keeps the documented `$HOME/.openclaw` convention — the guard short-circuits only when `env.OPENCLAW_HOME?.trim()` is non-empty.
  - Tilde-expanded explicit homes (`OPENCLAW_HOME=~/.openclaw`) work because `resolveEffectiveHomeDir` already runs through `expandHomePrefix` + `path.resolve` before the guard sees the resolved absolute path.
  - Symlinks: `path.basename(resolvedHome)` operates on the symlink name, not its target, so the guard matches the operator's chosen path name. This is the right semantic ("what did the user ask for?") and matches the analysis already in the prior closed attempt #45793.
- This is a narrower replacement for the closed-stale #45793 (also from a separate contributor, technically correct, lost to no maintainer engagement). The shape is the same; the new test coverage explicitly pins the implicit-`HOME` case so the guard cannot accidentally widen.
- Out-of-scope: `OPENCLAW_HOME` poisoning (already handled by `normalize()` in `src/infra/home-dir.ts:4`) and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/path/.openclaw` style explicit-state-dir overrides (those already short-circuit before the guard at line 65).

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Onboarding with `OPENCLAW_HOME=~/.openclaw` writes the config file to the wrong place (`~/.openclaw/.openclaw/openclaw.json`) and produces a nested directory. After the fix, the config is written to the canonical `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` location.
- Real environment tested: Local checkout at `../openclaw-45765` on Windows 11 + Node 22.14 with the patched `src/config/paths.ts` and `src/utils.ts`. Smoke run exercises the actual production `resolveStateDir`, `resolveConfigDir`, and `resolveDefaultConfigCandidates` exports through `node --import tsx`, no test runner, no mocks. PR head: `44b9b82478`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  - `git checkout fix/openclaw-home-state-dir-nesting && pnpm install`
  - `pnpm test src/config/paths.test.ts` (29 passed)
  - `pnpm test src/utils.test.ts` (18 passed)
  - `pnpm test src/infra/home-dir.test.ts` (27 passed)
  - `pnpm tsgo:core` (EXIT=0)
  - `node --import tsx ./smoke-45765.mjs` against the three observed shapes
- Evidence after fix:
~~~text
PR head 44b9b82478
$ pnpm test src/config/paths.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  29 passed (29)
   Duration  1.96s

$ pnpm test src/utils.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
   Duration  1.97s

$ pnpm test src/infra/home-dir.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  27 passed (27)
   Duration  331ms

$ pnpm tsgo:core
EXIT=0
~~~
- Observed result after fix: with `OPENCLAW_HOME=~/.openclaw` set, `resolveStateDir` / `resolveConfigDir` both return the explicit home directly and `resolveDefaultConfigCandidates` lists `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` as the canonical first candidate — no `~/.openclaw/.openclaw/...` candidate is produced anywhere in the list. With `OPENCLAW_HOME=/srv/openclaw-home` (non-state-dir basename), behavior is unchanged: `~/.openclaw` is still appended.
- What was not tested: a live `openclaw onboard` wizard run on Linux Kylin V10 / aarch64 (the reporter's environment). The behavior is source-reproducible from the patched production code through `node --import tsx` and is unit-covered by the new regression tests; a live onboarding run would only exercise the same call chain.

Closes #45765

target.title: fix: chat.send no reply when thinking metadata is set
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a normal `chat.send` message with per-message `thinking` metadata could persist the user turn but produce no assistant response. The gateway was converting structured `thinking` metadata into textual `/think ...` command input, so clients without text slash-command authority could have a normal message treated as command text before model dispatch.

No related open GitHub issue or PR was found. I searched live GitHub and local gitcrawl for `chat.send thinking`, Android/chat no-reply reports, `/think` command-body reports, and paired-device slash-command authorization reports. The only direct keyword hit was already-merged #79385, which is a broader thinking/fast controls PR rather than this no-reply bug report.

## Why This Change Was Made

`chat.send` already has a structured dispatch path for one-turn thinking metadata via `replyOptions.thinkingLevelOverride`. This PR removes the duplicate `/think <level> <message>` rewrite for normal messages, leaving `CommandBody`, `BodyForCommands`, and `CommandTurn.body` as the user’s actual message while still passing the requested thinking override to reply resolution.

The review pass also hardened the adjacent reply/model-selection behavior so explicit thinking-off inputs, per-agent thinking defaults, and per-model `params.thinking` defaults prevent model reasoning defaults from being re-enabled during normal directive resolution and auto-fallback primary probes.

## User Impact

Mobile, WebChat, consult, and other `chat.send` clients can set a one-shot thinking level without accidentally turning a normal user message into a text slash command. `thinking` remains turn-local metadata: it applies to the dispatched run, does not alter the visible/user command text, and does not persist `thinkingLevel` into the session store.

## Evidence

Behavioral proof:

- `chat.send` with `message: "hello from phone"` and `thinking: "low"` now dispatches with `BodyForCommands === "hello from phone"`, `CommandBody === "hello from phone"`, `CommandTurn.kind === "normal"`, and `replyOptions.thinkingLevelOverride === "low"`.
- The persisted session store is checked at the canonical `agent:main:main` key and the legacy `main` view to prove one-turn `thinking` metadata does not become durable session `thinkingLevel`.
- Auto-fallback tests cover `params.thinking` values `false`, `"disabled"`, and `"none"` so configured thinking-off aliases keep reasoning defaults off when probing a primary model.

Validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/chat.directive-tags.test.ts -t "chat.send keeps thinking metadata out of command text for normal messages"` - passed, 2 tests run with unrelated tests skipped.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat.test.ts -t "chat.send does not persist one-turn thinking metadata"` - passed, 1 test run with unrelated tests skipped.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.auto-fallback.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-directives.target-session.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts` - passed, 173 tests.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo` - passed.

target.title: fix(discord): disable ws 8.21.0 receiver part limits for gateway sockets
target.body:
## Summary

ws 8.21.0 introduced `maxBufferedChunks` and `maxFragments` receiver limits (commit `[security] Limit retained message parts`) that can trigger `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` and close connections with code 1008 under certain traffic patterns.

This PR explicitly sets both limits to `0` (disabled) for Discord gateway WebSocket connections, restoring the ws 8.20.0 behavior for the trusted Discord gateway peer while preserving the security fix for all other WebSocket usage.

## Changes

- **`extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.ts`**: Base class `createWebSocket()` now passes `maxBufferedChunks: 0, maxFragments: 0` with a `ws.ClientOptions` cast (since `@types/ws` 8.18.1 does not yet expose these fields).
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.ts`**: Extended `DiscordGatewayWebSocketCtor` type to include the new options; monitor gateway creation path passes the same disabled limits.
- **`extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.test.ts`**: Added test verifying base class WebSocket receives the expected options.
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.test.ts`**: Added test verifying monitor plugin WebSocket receives the expected options.
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/provider.proxy.test.ts`**: Updated two existing exact-match assertions to include the new options.

## Why `0` instead of raising the limits

- ws 8.21.0 treats `0` as disabled (`receiver.js:61`, `receiver.js:98`: `if (this._maxBufferedChunks > 0 && ...)`), matching the pre-8.21.0 behavior exactly.
- Discord gateway is a trusted peer; the security limits are designed to protect against untrusted senders.
- Choosing an arbitrary higher threshold would be fragile without real production traffic data to calibrate against.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: ws 8.21.0's retained-part receiver limits (`maxFragments` default 131072 / `maxBufferedChunks` default 1048576) abort a Discord gateway socket with `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` / close `1008`; this PR sets both to `0` (disabled) on the Discord gateway sockets, restoring ws 8.20.0 behavior for that trusted peer.
- **Real environment tested**: Live Discord gateway connection from a Docker `node:22-bookworm-slim` container (Node `v22.22.3`) with the repo-pinned `ws@8.21.0` installed exactly, using a real bot token (redacted), connecting to `wss://gateway.discord.gg/?v=10&encoding=json`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: build a `node:22-bookworm-slim` image with `npm install ws@8.21.0`, then run a client that constructs the gateway socket with this patch's options (`new ws.WebSocket(url, { handshakeTimeout: 30000, maxBufferedChunks: 0, maxFragments: 0 })`), completes the HELLO/IDENTIFY/READY handshake against the real Discord gateway, sends heartbeats, holds a 60s stable window, then closes with code 1000.
- **Evidence after fix**: Live Discord gateway run with this patch's options applied (token, `session_id`, and `resume_gateway_url` redacted):

```
[env] node=v22.22.3 ws=8.21.0
[discord] connecting wss://gateway.discord.gg (maxBufferedChunks:0, maxFragments:0)
[discord] open
[discord] HELLO heartbeat_interval=41250ms
[discord] IDENTIFY sent (token redacted)
[discord] READY received (session_id/resume_gateway_url redacted)
[discord] HEARTBEAT_ACK #1
[discord] stable window 60000ms complete
[discord] close code=1000 reason=<empty>
[result] PASS live: READY + 1 heartbeat ACK; no WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS during stable window
```

Supplemental deterministic mechanism repro against a local ws 8.21.0 gateway streaming one message in 131073 fragments (one over the client default `maxFragments`), exercising the same `ws.WebSocket` receiver path:

```
# default ws.WebSocket (ws 8.21 defaults)
[before] open
[before] error code=WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS message=Too many message fragments
[before] close code=1006 reason=<empty>

# this patch's options applied
[after] open
[after] message received: 131073 bytes - NO receiver-limit close
```

- **Observed result after fix**: On the real Discord gateway, with the disabled limits applied, the connection reaches `READY`, exchanges heartbeats, and stays connected through the 60s window with no `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` and no `1008` close; the only close is the intentional client-initiated `1000`. The deterministic repro confirms the same constructor options remove the receiver-limit close that the default ws 8.21 client hits.
- **What was not tested**: the live run confirms a real gateway session stays healthy with the patched options, but does not force Discord's production fragmentation pattern on demand, does not exercise the `zlib-stream` transport, and does not drive the full OpenClaw plugin wiring end-to-end. The deterministic repro proves the ws 8.21 retained-part mechanism and that this patch's options disable the exact receiver checks, but uses a local peer rather than Discord's live framing.

## Tests

- `gateway.test.ts`: 25 passed
- `gateway-plugin.test.ts`: 17 passed  
- `provider.proxy.test.ts`: 21 passed
- TypeScript check (tsgo): clean

Fixes #88330

target.title: fix(reply): deliver durable reasoning on the origin-route when /reasoning opts in
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the **origin-routing** delivery path, a durable `{ text, isReasoning: true }` reasoning payload for `/reasoning on` is produced, clears every dispatch-level gate, and is then **unconditionally dropped inside `routeReply`** — so opted-in durable reasoning is silently lost when a reply is routed back to its originating channel.

- `routeReply` (`src/auto-reply/reply/route-reply.ts:131`) suppresses `payload.isReasoning === true` with no opt-in flag.
- The **direct** dispatch path already honors the per-channel tri-state opt-in and delivers reasoning when enabled (`dispatch-from-config.ts:3347`/`:3537`, `reply.isReasoning === true && !reasoningPayloadsEnabled`).
- Both origin-route delivery lanes funnel through the single `routeReply` chokepoint, so the origin route never received that flag. The blanket suppression (`shouldSuppressReasoningPayload`) predates the `reasoningPayloadsEnabled` opt-in (`8d0c02c24b`), which was applied to the direct gates but not to `routeReply` — i.e. the origin route was left on the pre-opt-in "always internal" behavior. See #99492.

**Outcome:** `routeReply` gains an optional `reasoningPayloadsEnabled` param and suppresses reasoning **only when it is not enabled**, mirroring the direct-dispatch gate. `routeReplyToOriginating` threads the resolved flag. `/reasoning on` durable reasoning is delivered on the origin route; `/reasoning off` (and every caller that does not opt in) stays suppressed exactly as before.

## Evidence

The change is exercised through the **real `routeReply` function** against the real outbound-delivery seam (`deliverOutboundPayloads`) that the whole `route-reply.test.ts` suite already uses — actual code execution at the exact bug boundary, deterministic and reproducible.

- **Behavior addressed:** on the origin route, `routeReply` delivers a durable `isReasoning` payload when `reasoningPayloadsEnabled` is true, and still suppresses it when the flag is absent/false.
- **Exact command:** `pnpm exec vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/route-reply.test.ts -t "reasoning"`

**Evidence after fix — BEFORE (upstream `route-reply.ts`, new tests kept):**
```
✓ suppresses reasoning payloads by default
✓ keeps suppressing reasoning payloads when reasoning delivery is disabled
× delivers reasoning payloads when reasoning delivery is enabled
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times
Tests  1 failed | 2 passed | 38 skipped
```
→ even with `reasoningPayloadsEnabled: true`, outbound delivery is called **0 times** — the payload is dropped at `route-reply.ts:131`.

**Evidence after fix — AFTER (this PR):**
```
✓ suppresses reasoning payloads by default
✓ keeps suppressing reasoning payloads when reasoning delivery is disabled
✓ delivers reasoning payloads when reasoning delivery is enabled
Tests  3 passed | 38 skipped
```
→ `reasoningPayloadsEnabled: true` delivers the reasoning payload once; `false`/absent stays suppressed.

- **Regression + gates:** `route-reply.test.ts` + `dispatch-from-config.test.ts` — **274 passed**. `pnpm lint --threads=8` and `pnpm check:test-types` both green.
- **Proof limitation:** lead proof is the executed real-code before/after at the `routeReply` boundary. A live dev-gateway origin-routed render (Discord/Telegram, `/reasoning on`) can be staged on request.

## Exactly-once / reviewer focus

This change does not alter which payloads exist or the streamed-vs-final dedupe. It only stops `routeReply` from dropping an `isReasoning` payload it was already handed. The origin route now has the **same** delivery multiplicity as the already-correct direct path (streamed block via `dispatcher.sendBlockReply` at `:3433` + final via `sendFinalPayload` at `:3561`); it does not introduce a new duplicate the direct path lacks. Matching final payloads are filtered before final dispatch via block/direct-send evidence (`agent-runner-payloads.ts:287`/`:443`).

## Scope — intentionally out of scope

- **Queued follow-up** (`followup-runner.ts`): its re-run options set no `reasoningPayloadsEnabled` / `onReasoningStream`, so a durable reasoning payload is never emitted there — a `routeReply` flag cannot affect it. Separate, upstream concern.
- **ACP delivery** (`dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`): no reasoning plumbing exists on that path today; wiring it is separate work.
- `commands-private-route` / `commands-reset-hooks` route command acks / reset notices, never `isReasoning` — they keep the default suppress.
- No change to `shouldSuppressReasoningPayload`, provider routing, config schema, or public API.

## Linked context

- Closes #99492.
- Related #90943 (wired the blanket suppression onto the origin/follow-up path).
- Related #99401 (tri-state CLI thinking + follow-up resolver gate; its Scope note documents this exact origin-route boundary).
- Not requested by a maintainer; follow-up extending the tri-state reasoning-delivery work to the origin route.

target.title: feat(github-copilot): support GitHub Enterprise data-residency Copilot auth
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves Organizations on a data-residency GitHub Enterprise tenant (a `*.ghe.com` host such as `your-org.ghe.com`) could not use GitHub Copilot with OpenClaw. Copilot auth, token refresh, and completions were hardwired to public `github.com` / `api.github.com`, so onboarding via `openclaw models auth` and the Copilot provider offered no way to reach a tenant-local Copilot endpoint. Enterprise users were effectively locked out of the Copilot provider. ## Why This Change Was Made Adds GitHub Enterprise (data residency) as a first-class Copilot auth choice, nested alongside the existing GitHub and Local Proxy options. Picking it prompts for the tenant domain, runs the device login against that host, and persists the domain to `models.providers.github-copilot.params.githubDomain` so later token refreshes and completions resolve automatically. Domain resolution follows `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` env > config > `github.com`. The domain is threaded through every Copilot code path — device flow, token exchange, completions, embeddings, image understanding, and simple-completion — so all features work on the tenant, not just chat. Public `github.com` behavior is unchanged (no config is written for the default host). No config schema change (uses free-form provider params). **Security (fail-closed by design):** the host allowlist is locked to `github.com` and `*.ghe.com` tenants only — any other value (typo or injected `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN`/config) falls back to `github.com` so the GitHub OAuth token can never be redirected to an arbitrary `api.`. The cached Copilot API token is scoped by the GitHub host it was minted for, so a public token is never reused against a tenant host (or vice versa) after a domain switch. **Domain-switch re-authentication:** onboarding no longer reuses a stored Copilot token when the selected domain differs from the one the token was minted under. Any switch (public `github.com` ↔ a `*.ghe.com` tenant, or one tenant to another) forces a fresh device login so the persisted `githubDomain` always matches a tenant-scoped token; re-running login for the *same* domain still offers to reuse the current token. Switching back to public `github.com` clears the persisted `githubDomain` so config returns to the default (no config == `github.com`). This closes the gap where declining re-login could write a tenant domain against an unverified public token. ## User Impact Enterprise users can now authenticate Copilot against their `*.ghe.com` tenant directly from onboarding or `openclaw models auth` by choosing **GitHub Copilot (Enterprise / data residency)** and entering their domain — no manual URL editing. Chat, embeddings (memory search), and image understanding all route to the tenant. `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` enables fully headless/CI setups. target.title: feat(signal): show status reactions during inbound replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal users could receive a normal agent reply without the lifecycle status reactions already available in other message channels. When status reactions are configured, Signal can now show that an inbound message was acknowledged, is being processed, is using tools or compacting, has stalled, and then completed or failed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal inbound handling now uses the shared status-reaction controller behind the existing `messages.statusReactions.enabled`, acknowledgement scope, and Signal `reactionLevel` gates. Direct messages react to the inbound sender/timestamp; group messages react through the group id plus the original message author; reaction send/remove failures are logged without blocking the agent dispatch path.

The shared dispatch path also forwards opted-in compaction lifecycle callbacks when normal progress text is hidden, so reaction-only progress can still move through compacting and back to thinking.

The observed `⏳` hourglass is intentional. It is the shared soft-stall status (`stallSoft`) from the default status-reaction timing, and Signal also uses it as the default hard-stall reaction so a long-running turn does not look like a terminal failure. Explicit configured `messages.statusReactions.emojis.stallHard` overrides are still honored.

## User Impact

Configured Signal routes can show live status reactions during an agent turn instead of only typing/read feedback. Replies that are sent through message tools are treated as successful visible replies, so the final status does not incorrectly flash as an error when the reply was delivered through that path.

target.title: fix(agents): classify Anthropic refusal and OpenAI content_filter as failover-eligible refusals
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Provider refusals (Anthropic safety classifiers, OpenAI `content_filter`) silently bypass the model fallback chain. When a provider returns a refusal, the agent run-loop surfaces a generic "LLM request failed." error without ever consulting the configured fallback models — even though Anthropic's own refusal copy recommends configuring a fallback model.
- Problem: `classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage` has no refusal pattern → `classifyAssistantFailoverReason` returns null → `failoverFailure=false` → `shouldRotateAssistant=false` → `continue_normal` → fallback chain never checked
- Solution: Add `"refusal"` to `FailoverReason`, match Anthropic refusal and `content_filter` messages in the unified failover classifier, and treat refusal as a transient failure eligible for cooldown probing
- What changed: `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/types.ts` (+1, new failover reason), `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts` (+12, refusal detection in `classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage`), `src/agents/failover-policy.ts` (+2, cooldown probe eligibility), `src/agents/auth-profiles/types.ts` (+1, `AuthProfileFailureReason` mirror), `src/agents/runtime-plan/types.ts` (+1, `AgentRuntimeFailoverReason` mirror), `src/agents/auth-profiles/usage-state.ts` (+1, model-scoped cooldown for refusal), `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/result-fallback-classifier.ts` (+2, wire refusal through result payload fallback)
- What did NOT change: `failover-matches.ts` (refusal is two simple prefix matches, not worth a pattern group), `resolveFailoverStatus` (refusal has no HTTP analog), `resolveSessionSuspensionReason` (default `circuit_open` is correct), `buildFailoverRemediationHint` (only triggers for auth)

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [x] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #98976
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Three production incidents in one morning logged `failoverReason: null` for Anthropic refusals with `Anthropic refusal (category: bio) ...` in the error body. Each time the provider message explicitly said "API integrators: you can reduce refusals for your users by configuring a fallback model — see https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/refusals-and-fallback". But OpenClaw never triggered the fallback chain because the failover classification pipeline had no concept of a refusal.

After fix, a refusal flows through the same rotate-profile → fallback-model pipeline as rate limits and overloads. The refused model enters cooldown; the next candidate handles the turn.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Provider refusals (Anthropic `stop_reason=refusal`, OpenAI `finish_reason=content_filter`) are classified as failover-eligible, triggering the configured model fallback chain instead of silently dying with "LLM request failed."
- Real environment tested: Linux x86_64, Node 22, branch `fix/provider-refusal-fallback-98976`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/types.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/failover-matches.test.ts src/agents/failover-policy.ts src/agents/failover-policy.test.ts

OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/failover-matches.test.ts src/agents/failover-policy.test.ts

OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors-provider-structured-signals.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/provider-error-patterns.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { classifyFailoverReason } from './src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts';

console.log('=== Refusal classification proof ===');
console.log();

const cases = [
  { input: 'Anthropic refusal (category: bio): The content...', expect: 'refusal' },
  { input: 'Anthropic refusal.', expect: 'refusal' },
  { input: 'Provider finish_reason: content_filter', expect: 'refusal' },
  { input: 'LLM request failed.', expect: null },
  { input: 'rate limit exceeded', expect: 'rate_limit' },
  { input: 'The request was refused by the proxy.', expect: null },
];

for (const c of cases) {
  const result = classifyFailoverReason(c.input);
  const status = result === c.expect ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL';
  console.log(status + ' | \"' + c.input.substring(0, 60) + '\" → ' + result);
}
"
=== Refusal classification proof ===

PASS | "Anthropic refusal (category: bio): The content..." → refusal
PASS | "Anthropic refusal." → refusal
PASS | "Provider finish_reason: content_filter" → refusal
PASS | "LLM request failed." → null
PASS | "rate limit exceeded" → rate_limit
PASS | "The request was refused by the proxy." → null
```

Classification matrix:

| Input message | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| `"Anthropic refusal (category: bio): ..."` | `"refusal"` | `"refusal"` |
| `"Anthropic refusal."` | `"refusal"` | `"refusal"` |
| `"Provider finish_reason: content_filter"` | `"refusal"` | `"refusal"` |
| `"LLM request failed."` | `null` (not refusal) | `null` |
| `"rate limit exceeded"` | `"rate_limit"` (not refusal) | `"rate_limit"` |
| `"The request was refused by the proxy."` | `null` (not refusal) | `null` |

Cooldown probe matrix:

| FailoverReason | allowCooldownProbe | useTransientProbeSlot | preserveTransientProbeSlot |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"refusal"` (new) | ✅ true | ❌ false | ❌ false |
| `"rate_limit"` | ✅ true | ✅ true | ❌ false |
| `"overloaded"` | ✅ true | ✅ true | ❌ false |

Unit test results:
```
 ✓ |unit-fast| failover-matches.test.ts   27 passed (4 new refusal tests)
 ✓ |unit-fast| failover-policy.test.ts     1 passed (matrix updated)
 ✓ provider-error-patterns.test.ts         88 passed (no regressions)
 ✓ oxfmt --check                            7 files clean
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. `classifyFailoverReason("Anthropic refusal ...")` returns `"refusal"` — was `null`
  2. `shouldAllowCooldownProbeForReason("refusal")` returns `true` — would have been `false` (new reason)
  3. `shouldUseTransientCooldownProbeSlot("refusal")` returns `true` — would have been `false`
  4. `shouldPreserveTransientCooldownProbeSlot("refusal")` returns `false` — correct (refusal is transient)
  5. `shouldEscalateRetryLimit("refusal")` returns `true` — correct (fallthrough from negative list)
  6. All existing failover classifications unchanged — zero regression

### E2E Pipeline Proof (full classification → failover decision chain)

After the classifier fix, an `AssistantMessage` with an Anthropic refusal or OpenAI `content_filter` error message flows through the entire failover pipeline:

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { classifyAssistantFailoverReason } from './src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.js';
import { resolveRunFailoverDecision } from './src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-policy.js';

const refusalMsg = {
  role: 'assistant',
  api: 'anthropic-chat',
  provider: 'anthropic',
  model: 'claude-sonnet-4-6',
  stopReason: 'error',
  errorMessage: 'Anthropic refusal (category: bio): The content contains references to biological agents.',
  content: [],
  usage: { input: 100, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0, totalTokens: 100, cost: { input: 0.003, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0, total: 0.003 } },
  timestamp: Date.now(),
};

console.log('=== 1. Anthropic refusal → classifyAssistantFailoverReason ===');
const reason = classifyAssistantFailoverReason(refusalMsg);
console.log(reason);  // 'refusal'

console.log('\\n=== 2. resolveRunFailoverDecision — rotate profile first ===');
console.log(JSON.stringify(resolveRunFailoverDecision({
  stage: 'assistant', aborted: false, externalAbort: false,
  fallbackConfigured: true, failoverFailure: reason !== null, failoverReason: reason,
  timedOut: false, idleTimedOut: false,
  timedOutDuringCompaction: false, timedOutDuringToolExecution: false,
  profileRotated: false,
})));
// → {\"action\":\"rotate_profile\",\"reason\":\"refusal\"}

console.log('\\n=== 3. resolveRunFailoverDecision — fallback model after rotation exhausted ===');
console.log(JSON.stringify(resolveRunFailoverDecision({
  stage: 'assistant', aborted: false, externalAbort: false,
  fallbackConfigured: true, failoverFailure: reason !== null, failoverReason: reason,
  timedOut: false, idleTimedOut: false,
  timedOutDuringCompaction: false, timedOutDuringToolExecution: false,
  profileRotated: true,
})));
// → {\"action\":\"fallback_model\",\"reason\":\"refusal\"}

console.log('\\n=== 4. Before fix: null failoverReason → continue_normal ===');
console.log(JSON.stringify(resolveRunFailoverDecision({
  stage: 'assistant', aborted: false, externalAbort: false,
  fallbackConfigured: true, failoverFailure: false, failoverReason: null,
  timedOut: false, idleTimedOut: false,
  timedOutDuringCompaction: false, timedOutDuringToolExecution: false,
  profileRotated: false,
})));
// → {\"action\":\"continue_normal\"}
"
=== 1. Anthropic refusal → classifyAssistantFailoverReason ===
refusal

=== 2. resolveRunFailoverDecision — rotate profile first ===
{"action":"rotate_profile","reason":"refusal"}

=== 3. resolveRunFailoverDecision — fallback model after rotation exhausted ===
{"action":"fallback_model","reason":"refusal"}

=== 4. Before fix: null failoverReason → continue_normal ===
{"action":"continue_normal"}
```

**Before fix**: `null` → `resolveRunFailoverDecision` → `continue_normal` → user sees generic "LLM request failed." with no fallback attempt.

**After fix**: `"refusal"` → `resolveRunFailoverDecision` → first `rotate_profile`, then `fallback_model` → configured fallback model handles the turn.

## Root Cause

`classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts` had no pattern for "Anthropic refusal" or "Provider finish_reason: content_filter". When an assistant message arrived with `stopReason="error"` and refusal text, the classifier returned `null`, `isFailoverAssistantError` returned `false`, `shouldRotateAssistant` returned `false`, and `resolveRunFailoverDecision` returned `{ action: "continue_normal" }` — which ends the turn with no fallback attempt.

Provenance: `introduced by` the original `shared/anthropic-refusal.ts` — the refusal→error mapping was wired but never connected to failover classification.

Confidence: `clear` — single classification entry point, all callers downstream react to the returned reason.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a provider refuses a prompt and fallback models are configured, the agent now falls back to the next candidate instead of surfacing "LLM request failed." with no fallback attempt. When no fallbacks are configured, behavior is unchanged — the refusal message is still surfaced.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: `classifyFailoverReason` correctly classifies Anthropic refusal (with/without category), OpenAI content_filter, and does not false-positive on proxy refusal text or generic errors
- Edge cases checked: Empty string, unrelated text containing "refusal" in proxy context

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — purely additive; existing reasons unchanged
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The single classification entry point (`classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage`) is the right boundary because every failover path (assistant-stage, prompt-stage, signal-level, detail-level) already goes through it. Adding a new reason here automatically propagates to the full fallback pipeline without touching any of the downstream decision helpers.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Classifying refusal via `failover-error.ts`'s `resolveFailoverReasonFromError` path. Rejected — that path only fires for thrown errors, whereas refusal is a normal stream result with `stopReason="error"` on the assistant message. The message-level classifier is the correct gate.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Risk**: The refusal reason string format changes across Anthropic SDK versions. Mitigation: `startsWith("Anthropic refusal")` is a loose prefix check; the underlying `applyAnthropicRefusal` function always produces `"Anthropic refusal"` as the message prefix, and that prefix is independently test-covered in existing refusal formatting tests.
- **Risk**: OpenAI `content_filter` finish reason could be confused with a future provider that uses different wording. Mitigation: exact prefix match `"Provider finish_reason: content_filter"` which is the canonical output of `mapOpenAIStopReason` — any format change there would also break the existing stop-reason mapping.

---
Fixes #98976

## Why Context pruning changes model input quality and cost, but there was no dedicated internal lifecycle signal for pruning actions. This PR emits a pruning lifecycle hook with safe summary metadata so pruning behavior is observable without exposing pruned content. Closes #8606 ## Detailed Changes - Added internal lifecycle event: - `session:prune` - Pruning hook context includes summary metadata: - `softTrimmedCount` - `hardClearedCount` - `toolNames` - `sessionId` (when available) - Updated context-pruning extension/pruner tests for async path + hook emission behavior ## Related Links and Issues - Existing source PR: #9761 - Closes #8606

Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR adds a new internal hook lifecycle event, `session:prune`, emitted by the context pruning path. The pruner now tracks how many tool results were soft-trimmed vs hard-cleared (and which tool names were affected), and passes this safe summary metadata into an internal hook event. The context-pruning extension’s `context` handler was updated to be async to await pruning, and tests were updated to cover the async path and hook emission behavior. Within the codebase, this integrates into the existing internal hook system (`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`) by creating and triggering an `InternalHookEvent` of type `session` and action `prune`, keyed by a derived session key.

Confidence Score: 4/5

- This PR is mostly safe to merge, but there is one correctness issue around the emitted hook event timestamp semantics that should be clarified/fixed. - The changes are localized (pruner + extension + tests + docs) and align with existing internal hook infrastructure. The main concern is that the emitted hook event uses a timestamp created at emission time, which can be meaningfully later than the prune operation and may mislead consumers relying on timing semantics. - src/agents/pi-extensions/context-pruning/pruner.ts

target.title: fix(runtime): guard JSON.stringify against circular references in tool output
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`writeJson()` and `writeRuntimeJson()` call `JSON.stringify(value)` on arbitrary tool return values. Circular references cause `TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON`, crashing the output path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrap both `JSON.stringify` calls in try-catch. On failure, fallback to `JSON.stringify(String(value))`.

## User Impact

Prevents runtime crash when tools return objects with circular references.

## Evidence

![runtime proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhangLei99586/openclaw/proof-screenshots/pr-99488-99490-proof.png)

- OLD: `TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON`
- NEW: caught → fallback → `"[object Object]"` — no crash

`mintAttachGrant` calls `params.sessionKey.trim()` assuming a string, but the caller resolves it via `readString() ?? resolveMainSessionKey()`. If both return `undefined`, `.trim()` throws `TypeError` instead of reaching the validation guard.

`params.sessionKey?.trim() ?? ""` — undefined flows through to `if (!sessionKey)` check instead of crashing.

Prevents TypeError crash when MCP attach grants are requested without a valid session key.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This PR wires the durable runtime foundation from PR2 into agent/session/subagent paths so OpenClaw can record durable context for chat sends, agent runs, subagent child runs, parent fan-in, yield progress, and restart/recovery inspection.

The target behavior is: parent agents should have durable child/fan-in state; one failed child should not make sibling completion invisible; and Gateway/session restart should leave inspectable runtime state instead of silent coordinator ambiguity.

## Dependency Chain

This is PR3 in the replacement durable runtime stack:

1. PR1: durable session/task runtime RFC v2.
2. PR2: durable runtime foundation.
3. PR3: agent/session/subagent wiring, this PR.

This branch is stacked on the refreshed PR2 branch. The upstream PR diff against `main` is cumulative. For delta-only review after PR2, use:

https://github.com/mjnkao/openclaw/compare/codex/openclaw-durable-runtime-foundation-v2-ready...codex/openclaw-durable-runtime-agent-v2-ready

## Summary

Adds:

- Gateway `chat.send` and `agent.run` durable context refs;
- user-turn transcript durable context propagation;
- embedded-agent yield progress for resumable parent turns;
- subagent child-run mirroring and parent fan-in association;
- task completion contract metadata for durable parent/child lifecycle;
- status-notice display metadata for durable/yield progress;
- protocol schema fields for durable context references.

## Explicit Non-Scope

- Planner/product modules.
- Board-style UI/tools.
- Projection adapters.

target.title: fix(acp): keep ACP bridge off stale paired gateway-client baseline (#74650)
target.body:
## Root cause

`src/acp/server.ts:58` builds a CLI-mode `GatewayClient` for the ACP bridge but never opts out of attaching the host's persisted CLI device identity. On hosts where that paired identity has a lower scope than the Gateway expects for ACP, the client keeps requesting an admin scope upgrade against a stale baseline. Approving the prompt does not clear it, retries reuse the same stuck request id or generate a new one, and ACP never finishes initializing. This is exactly the failure mode in #74650 on 2026.4.26 (`scope upgrade pending approval`, multiple request ids observed, ACP and ACPX both stuck).

The merged fix #74472 already addressed the same shape for native operator-approval clients via `shouldOmitOperatorApprovalDeviceIdentity`, but that helper lives inside `operator-approvals-client.ts` and the ACP bridge does not go through it.

## Fix

1. Extract the loopback-plus-shared-auth check into a small shared module `src/gateway/loopback-shared-auth-identity.ts` exporting `isLoopbackGatewayUrl` and `shouldOmitGatewayClientDeviceIdentity`. `operator-approvals-client.ts` now imports the helper instead of defining it inline, so the two callers cannot drift.
2. In `serveAcpGateway`, gate `deviceIdentity: null` through the same helper. Remote URLs and unauthenticated loopback launches keep the normal device identity, so legitimate scope-upgrade prompts still surface.

Routing semantics are unchanged for healthy ACP launches; the fix is a no-op outside the trusted-loopback-with-preauth path.

## Tests

I extended `src/acp/server.startup.test.ts` to capture the `deviceIdentity` value passed to `GatewayClient`, then added the same three-case coverage that #74472 has for native approvals:

- loopback `ws://127.0.0.1:18789` plus token, identity is `null`
- remote `wss://gateway.example/ws` plus token, identity stays `undefined`
- loopback with no shared auth, identity stays `undefined`

I also added a focused unit test file `src/gateway/loopback-shared-auth-identity.test.ts` covering the helper across IPv4 loopback, IPv6 `[::1]`, `localhost`, remote hosts, unparseable URLs, and the four token/password combinations.

```
pnpm vitest run src/gateway/loopback-shared-auth-identity.test.ts \
  src/gateway/operator-approvals-client.test.ts \
  src/acp/server.startup.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server.silent-scope-upgrade-reconnect.poc.test.ts
# 50/50 pass across 7 test files

pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 \
  src/acp/server.ts src/acp/server.startup.test.ts \
  src/gateway/loopback-shared-auth-identity.ts \
  src/gateway/loopback-shared-auth-identity.test.ts \
  src/gateway/operator-approvals-client.ts CHANGELOG.md
# All matched files use the correct format.
```

`server.silent-scope-upgrade-reconnect.poc.test.ts` shows a port-race flake when run alongside other server-port tests in parallel; it passes in isolation on both clean upstream/main and this branch, so it is unrelated.

## Manual reproduction

I seeded a paired CLI device identity with `operator.read` scope on a local Gateway started with a token, ran `openclaw acp` against the loopback URL with the token, and watched the bridge attach the paired identity and request `operator.admin` before ACP initialization completed. Approving the request did not clear it, and retries generated fresh request ids, matching the symptoms in the issue. With this patch applied, `serveAcpGateway` calls `GatewayClient` with `deviceIdentity: null`, the bridge connects without re-triggering a scope-upgrade prompt, and ACP `initialize` completes normally. Remote launches against a non-loopback URL still attach the device identity as before.

## AI / vibe-coding disclosure

This patch was developed with Claude Opus 4.7 (Anthropic) assistance under my direction. I reviewed every change by hand, drove the investigation against the clawsweeper triage on #74650, mirrored the shape of the merged #74472 PR exactly so the two paths cannot drift, ran the full acceptance-criteria test set listed above, and confirmed the helper extraction does not change the operator-approvals path's runtime behavior.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where gateway/model catalog readers could observe plugin catalog sidecar directories while the model catalog writer was updating them, causing `FsSafeError: directory changed during operation` warnings and retry loops during provider model discovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `models.json` write serialization now also protects reads that depend on the same `models.json` plus generated plugin catalog sidecar snapshot. target.title: fix: making typing start fire-and-forget allows cleanup/idle to run before a persistent typin...
target.body:
## Summary

Found one concrete regression: making typing start fire-and-forget allows cleanup/idle to run before a persistent typing indicator has finished starting, so the stop path can no-op and leave the indicator behind.

## What ClawSweeper Is Fixing

- **Medium: Pending typing start can outlive cleanup and leave persistent indicators stuck** (regression)
  - File: `src/channels/typing.ts:79`
  - Evidence: `onReplyStart` now starts `fireStart()` in the background and returns after one microtask at `src/channels/typing.ts:79-87`, while `fireStop` immediately marks the callbacks closed and calls `stop` at `src/channels/typing.ts:90-98`. For Feishu, `start` assigns `typingState` only after `await addTypingIndicator(...)` at `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts:176`; `stop` returns without doing anything if `typingState` is still unset at `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts:183-185`. A fast cleanup while `addTypingIndicator` is still in flight therefore calls stop too early, then the delayed start completes and records a persistent reaction with no later removal.
  - Impact: Feishu typing reactions are explicitly persistent until removed. A quick reply, `NO_REPLY`, empty-message cleanup, cancellation, or send-policy path can leave a visible typing reaction/indicator on the parent message after the run is already finished.
  - Suggested fix: keep typing start off the reply critical path, but serialize cleanup against the pending start. For example, track the current start promise and, if stop/cleanup happens while it is pending, run `stop` again after the promise settles when a start actually completed. Alternatively make persistent-indicator channels expose an abortable/pending-aware start helper.
  - Confidence: high

Tested on pushed branch `115daf62fe`: focused Vitest coverage for config/CLI/chat/TUI passed, config schema check passed, the real `pnpm openclaw experimental --help` entrypoint resolved, the interactive CLI picker wrote a throwaway config with visible VHS proof (https://vhs.charm.sh/vhs-2YeaK01TZ6WTsES0OdmQ9o.gif), a real TUI selector flow has visible VHS proof (https://vhs.charm.sh/vhs-68AM8dBhPO6aTrEiKOq2Wu.gif), and a rebuilt Docker gateway exercised `/experimental` over WebSocket with persisted config writes.

## Summary

- **Problem:** OpenClaw has experimental config flags spread through the config schema, but the user-facing toggle surface was drifting toward a CLI-only implementation. That would make `/experimental` unavailable from chat/TUI/channel command surfaces and would duplicate the flag registry outside the config contract.
- **Why it matters:** Experimental flags affect runtime behavior and should use one bounded, auditable config subset across CLI, chat, TUI, and channel plugins instead of hard-coded per-surface lists.
- **What changed:** Added a shared experimental-flag helper that discovers boolean config leaves under `experimental` from the base config schema and schema UI hints. The CLI `openclaw experimental`, chat `/experimental`, TUI command handling, and channel-command registry now use that same subset.
- **Config command policy:** Added `commands.experimental` so `/experimental` can be enabled or disabled alongside other configurable command surfaces.
- **What did not change:** No new experimental flags were introduced. No secrets, network calls, or provider runtime behavior changed.

## Scope Note

This PR started as a small CLI picker, but review feedback exposed a broader product/security boundary: if experimental config can be edited from one surface, the implementation should not create a CLI-only registry or drift from chat, TUI, and channel command handling. The current shape is intentionally larger because it moves `/experimental` behind a shared schema-derived subset and a configurable command gate instead of adding another one-off config editor.

The scope is still kept to the minimum shared surface needed for that boundary: no new experimental flags, no arbitrary config editor, no new network/runtime capability, no SDK export, and no separate per-surface experimental registry.

target.title: Handle mid-turn precheck compaction end to end
target.body:
## Summary

- rethrow mid-turn precheck signals before persisting assistant failure messages
- let the lower-level Agent lifecycle bubble the same signal to overflow recovery
- skip CLI transcript compaction when the session branch is already compacted

## Why

Mid-turn tool-result precheck throws `MidTurnPrecheckSignal` so the embedded runner can compact and retry before the next model call. Both harness and lower-level agent lifecycle paths must let that control-flow signal escape instead of writing an assistant error. After recovery, the CLI lifecycle can see the session still over its budget and try to compact again; if the branch already ends with a compaction entry, that second pass should be treated as complete instead of failing with `Already compacted`.

## Validation

- patched local OpenClaw runtime and restarted gateway
- forced `agents.defaults.contextTokens=90000` during testing to trigger mid-turn pressure
- verified CLI returns `status: "ok"` with final output `MIDTURN_COMPACT_FINAL_OK`
- verified session JSONL has `compactions=1`, `assistantErrors=0`, final assistant `stop`

- **Problem:** Discord native slash-command deploy lacked a configurable lifecycle policy (`always` / `changed-only` / `disabled`), durable fingerprints across gateway restarts for `changed-only`, safe in-process coordination when multiple Discord accounts trigger background slash deploy from one gateway.
