target.title: feat: add slash command picker in chat composer
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has many slash commands, but the chat composer did not provide an in-context way to discover, filter, and select them. Users had to know command names ahead of time, and invalid slash input could still reach send-time flows without clear composer-side handling.

This PR adds a slash command picker that opens when the user types `/`, supports category switching between commands and skills, filters results as the user types, and validates slash-style input before sending.

## Evidence

- Added focused Swift coverage for slash command picker state and send-time validation in `OpenClawKitTests/ChatViewModelTests.swift`.
- Added iOS gateway coverage in `apps/ios/Tests/IOSGatewayChatTransportTests.swift` for the command catalog transport surface.
- Captured UI screenshots from the implemented picker states:
  - Full picker: https://github.com/VicZhang6/openclaw/blob/assets/slash-screenshots/docs/assets/slash-panel-all.png?raw=true
  - Commands tab: https://github.com/VicZhang6/openclaw/blob/assets/slash-screenshots/docs/assets/slash-panel-commands.png?raw=true
  - Skills tab: https://github.com/VicZhang6/openclaw/blob/assets/slash-screenshots/docs/assets/slash-panel-skills.png?raw=true

## Design Philosophy

Since OpenClaw has many slash commands, the picker appears directly from the chat composer instead of requiring a separate reference page or memorized command names. The UI keeps the command name, description, and category visible so users can choose quickly without losing message context.

### Key Features

- **Instant trigger**: Type `/` to open the floating picker
- **Category tabs**: Switch between Commands and Skills views
- **Live filtering**: Start typing to filter the list in real time
- **Rich metadata**: Each item shows its name, description, and category badge
- **Send-time validation**: Invalid slash input is intercepted before sending

### Screenshots

**Full picker - all commands and skills**
![Slash Panel All](https://github.com/VicZhang6/openclaw/blob/assets/slash-screenshots/docs/assets/slash-panel-all.png?raw=true)

**Filtered to commands only**
![Slash Panel Commands](https://github.com/VicZhang6/openclaw/blob/assets/slash-screenshots/docs/assets/slash-panel-commands.png?raw=true)

**Filtered to skills only**
![Slash Panel Skills](https://github.com/VicZhang6/openclaw/blob/assets/slash-screenshots/docs/assets/slash-panel-skills.png?raw=true)


## Follow-up Evidence for bb1dba00e6

- Fixed the catalog request to include the active agent context derived from `agent:<id>:...` session keys before calling `commands.list`.
- Softened client-side slash validation so uncataloged slash-prefixed text continues through `chat.send`; the Gateway remains the final parser/authorizer.
- Added focused coverage for non-default-agent catalog loading and uncataloged slash send-path behavior.
- Local verification:
  - `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter "slash command"` passed.
  - `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter "unknown leading slash"` passed.
  - `xcodebuild test -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClaw -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17' -only-testing:OpenClawTests/IOSGatewayChatTransportTests` passed.
  - `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter ChatViewModelTests --no-parallel` still has existing async timeout failures outside the slash-command tests; all slash-command tests in that run passed.

target.title: fix: strip conda env marker from host tool runs
target.body:
Closes #99424

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running OpenClaw from an activated Conda environment could have OpenClaw-managed host tool subprocesses inherit `CONDA_PREFIX`. That active-environment marker can redirect Python package managers or nested tools into the parent environment even though the tool command itself does not show that coupling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing host exec env sanitizer already strips `VIRTUAL_ENV` from inherited and requested override env, but the same policy did not include `CONDA_PREFIX`. This change adds `CONDA_PREFIX` to the shared host env security policy, regenerates the macOS policy mirror, and extends the sanitizer/baseline tests so both inherited env and request-scoped overrides are covered.

This is intentionally limited to `CONDA_PREFIX`; it does not change `PATH` handling or add broad Conda-specific environment filtering.

## User Impact

Users can launch OpenClaw from a Conda-activated shell without that active environment marker leaking into OpenClaw-managed host subprocesses. Existing trusted inherited environment behavior remains unchanged except for this single marker.

## Evidence

- Before/source proof on current main:

  ```shell
  PS> git show origin/main:src/infra/host-env-security-policy.json | Select-String -Pattern 'VIRTUAL_ENV|CONDA_PREFIX'

      "VIRTUAL_ENV",
  ```

  `VIRTUAL_ENV` was covered, while `CONDA_PREFIX` was absent from the policy.

- After this patch:
  - `CONDA_PREFIX` is present in `src/infra/host-env-security-policy.json`.
  - `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/HostEnvSecurityPolicy.generated.swift` is regenerated from the shared policy.
  - `src/infra/host-env-security.test.ts` asserts inherited `CONDA_PREFIX` is stripped and requested `CONDA_PREFIX` overrides are rejected.
  - `src/infra/host-env-security.reported-baseline.test.ts` keeps the reported baseline count aligned.

- After-fix terminal proof from a Conda-activated shell on Windows:

  ```text
  PS> D:\anaconda\Scripts\conda.exe run -n base cmd.exe /d /c "pnpm exec tsx ...\conda-host-env-proof.ts"
  parent_CONDA_PREFIX=<set>
  sanitized_env_has_CONDA_PREFIX=false
  override_rejected_CONDA_PREFIX=true
  child_CONDA_PREFIX=<unset>
  child_OPENCLAW_CLI=1
  child_exit_status=0
  ```

  The probe runs in Conda `base`, exercises OpenClaw's host exec sanitizer from this PR branch, and launches a child process with the sanitized OpenClaw-managed env. The parent has `CONDA_PREFIX`; the OpenClaw-launched child does not.

- Commands run:
  - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/host-env-security.test.ts src/infra/host-env-security.reported-baseline.test.ts src/infra/host-env-security.policy-parity.test.ts` → 42 tests passed
  - `node scripts/generate-host-env-security-policy-swift.mjs --check` → OK
  - `pnpm exec oxlint src/infra/host-env-security.test.ts src/infra/host-env-security.reported-baseline.test.ts src/infra/host-env-security.policy-parity.test.ts` → clean
  - `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/infra/host-env-security-policy.json src/infra/host-env-security.reported-baseline.json src/infra/host-env-security.reported-baseline.test.ts src/infra/host-env-security.test.ts apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/HostEnvSecurityPolicy.generated.swift` → clean
  - `git diff --check` → clean
  - `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main` → `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`

What was not tested: a full interactive OpenClaw agent turn from Conda was not run. The terminal proof uses a real Conda-activated shell and the same OpenClaw host exec sanitizer boundary that manages inherited and requested env for OpenClaw-launched subprocesses.

target.title: fix(logging): redact Telegram bot tokens from timeout URLs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a fetch to the Telegram Bot API times out, the diagnostic log URL produced by `sanitizeTimeoutLogUrl` still exposes the bot token in the path segment (`/bot<TOKEN>/...`). While the function strips userinfo, query, and hash, it did not redact credential-bearing path segments. Downstream `redactSensitiveText` can be configured off and its token mask (`bot123…cdef`) still leaks part of the token.

Fixes #96982

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a purpose-built `redactBotTokenPath` function in `packages/net-policy/src/redact-sensitive-url.ts` that uses a strict regex (`TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_PATH_RE`) requiring 6+ digit bot ID + colon or `%3A` + 20+ character secret, keyed by hostname via a redactor registry. This avoids false matches on innocuous `/bot/settings`-style application routes. The redactor is called from both the URL-parsed and fallback-string paths of `sanitizeTimeoutLogUrl`.

## User Impact

target.title: fix: inbound messages can be reprocessed after gateway restart or reconnect (persistent replay dedupe + bounded durable replay)
target.body:
Fixes #97538
Part of #69208

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where inbound messages could be **reprocessed after a gateway restart or channel reconnect**, producing duplicate agent runs and, in the worst case, an unrecoverable re-delivery storm:

- **Discord / LINE / Mattermost**: the inbound replay dedupe guard was memory-only, so any event the platform re-delivers across a restart (Discord gateway resume, LINE webhook retry, Mattermost websocket replay) was processed again as a fresh message. Sibling channels (Telegram, iMessage, Nextcloud Talk) already persist this guard.
- **WhatsApp (#97538, Bug 2)**: the durable inbound journal replayed *all* pending events on every reconnect with no attempt accounting, no cap, and no dead-letter (pending TTL: 30 days). A poison event — e.g. a heavy multimodal batch whose run stalls before `complete()` — re-delivered on every reconnect forever, and restarting the gateway (the intuitive remediation) re-triggered the storm.

#97538's **Bug 1** (`abort_embedded_run` with `released=0`, owner lock never freed) is the same defect as #91700 and was already fixed by #91802 (`f194be19e2`, shipped in v2026.6.10/v2026.6.11); the reporter was on v2026.6.5. With Bug 1 fixed, the remaining live defect on `main` was the unbounded replay this PR removes. Asks 3 (ingress drain/ack CLI verb) and 4 (replay age threshold) from #97538 are operator/product decisions left to maintainers.

## Why This Change Was Made

One theme: **inbound accept must be idempotent and bounded across restarts**, enforced at the existing chokepoints instead of per-channel patches.

- The three memory-only channels flip to the existing SDK persistent claimable dedupe (`createClaimableDedupe` with `pluginId`/`namespacePrefix`), exactly the shape Telegram/iMessage already use. TTLs and in-memory caps are preserved per channel.
- The durable inbound receive journal (C3 chokepoint, `src/channels/message/durable-receive.ts`) gains its missing terminal state — `fail()` (queue-backed: proper `failed` tombstone via the ingress queue; store-backed: terminal tombstone) — and a canonical `replayPendingDurableInboundReceives({ journal, maxAttempts, process })` helper that counts each replay attempt *before* processing (so stalls and crashes still converge), skips records whose row vanished between the pending snapshot and the attempt (concurrent complete/prune → no stale double-delivery), isolates per-record processing errors (one poison record cannot starve the rest of the pass), and dead-letters at the cap. WhatsApp's inline replay loop is deleted in favor of the helper (`WHATSAPP_DURABLE_INBOUND_MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS = 5`, a bound on total delivery attempts). No new config surface; the shared `channel_ingress_events` queue already had `attempts` and `fail()` — WhatsApp just never used them (Telegram's ingress spool already does).
- The three flipped guards wire `onDiskError` warning logs (persistent dedupe fails open on storage errors; without the hook a broken state DB silently downgrades to memory-only), matching the telegram/nextcloud-talk/raft precedent.
- Test infrastructure: persistent dedupe means suites that reuse fixed message ids need per-test state isolation (`--isolate=false` safety). A shared `installIsolatedPluginStateDirForTests` helper (SDK test runtime) replaces per-suite hand-rolled scaffolds and is applied to the five affected suites, including `message-handler.bot-self-filter.test.ts` which was committing fixed ids through the real guard.

Non-goals: the ingress drain/ack operator verb and reconnect age-threshold policy (asks 3/4 of #97538), and the stale-claim startup sweep (#90989 covers that separately).

Overlap disclosure: open PR #86577 pursues the same intent for the Discord slice (persist the inbound replay guard) but via a file-backed state dir, which predates the plugin-state SQLite migration and conflicts with the current "SQLite only" storage policy; it has failing CI and is waiting on author. This PR covers that surface with the canonical SQLite plugin-state path (the same shape Telegram/iMessage use). If this lands, #86577 should be closed as superseded.

## User Impact

- Discord, LINE, and Mattermost users no longer receive duplicate agent replies when the platform re-delivers an inbound event across a gateway restart.
- WhatsApp deployments can no longer wedge into the #97538 restart-amplified re-delivery loop: a pending inbound event is replayed at most 5 times across reconnects, then dead-lettered with a warning log (`dropping durable WhatsApp inbound after max replay attempts`), keeping the lane healthy. Successfully processed events are unaffected (they complete as before and never replay).

## Evidence

- TDD: every fix landed RED→GREEN.
  - `extensions/discord/src/monitor/inbound-dedupe.test.ts`, `extensions/line/src/webhook-replay-persist.test.ts`, `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/inbound-replay-persist.test.ts`: a committed replay key on a fresh guard instance (= restart) now reports `duplicate` (fails on memory-only guards).
  - `src/channels/message/durable-receive.test.ts` (+6): `fail()` dead-letters on both journal flavors and blocks re-accept; bounded replay processes fresh records, records attempts across stalled replays (`attempts` 1 → 2 → dead-letter at cap), dead-letters poison events, isolates a throwing record while still replaying the rest, and skips a record whose row vanished before the attempt was recorded.
- Suites: WhatsApp **979/979**, Discord **1810/1810**, LINE **292/292**, `src/channels/message/` **171/171**, `src/plugin-state/` **34/34**; mattermost green except `client.retry.test.ts`, which fails identically on the branch base `6cb82eaab8` (pre-existing, unrelated HTTP-retry suite).
- `pnpm build` clean; `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions:test` clean; `plugin-sdk:api:check` OK (baseline regenerated for the new exports); oxfmt/oxlint clean.
- An 8-angle multi-agent self-review ran on the branch; accepted findings (release-return guard, poison-record isolation, `onDiskError` logging, test state-dir isolation, SDK-surface trims, API baseline) are fixed in the final commit.
- `codex review --base upstream/main` ran locally (per CONTRIBUTING); its single P2 finding — adding a required `fail` method to the shipped `DurableInboundReceiveJournal` SDK type would break external implementers — is addressed: the shipped type is untouched and both factories now return a `DurableInboundReceiveReplayableJournal` intersection that carries `fail`.
- Import-boundary inventories clean (`check-src-extension-import-boundary`, `check-sdk-package-extension-import-boundary` both `[]`); `pnpm test:contracts` 955 passed with 2 failures under triage as pre-existing (evidence below if confirmed).
- Pre-existing, unrelated failure noted for reviewers: `src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-shared.test.ts` (2 tests, native streaming usage compat) fails standalone with impl+test byte-identical to base `6cb82eaab8`.
- Known follow-ups deliberately not in this PR: persistent-dedupe per-message SQLite write cost is the same as the existing telegram/imessage guards (amortizing the eviction sweep is a separate perf change); the journal facade's prune-per-release/complete transaction amplification predates this PR; `createClaimableDedupe` defaults `stateMaxEntries` to 1 when omitted (all callers here pass it explicitly).

**Real gateway restart-replay proof** (details + logs in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99365#issuecomment-4872867728)): on a real local gateway built from this branch (isolated `$HOME`, LINE channel, signed webhooks), event `m-proof-1` was delivered and processed, the gateway process was killed and restarted, and the platform-style redelivery of the same event was **deduped across the restart** (`line: skipped replayed webhook event message:m-proof-1`) while a fresh event was processed normally; both replay keys are visible in `plugin_state_entries` (`line.webhook-replay.*`). Discord/Mattermost flip the identical mechanism.

**Why the WhatsApp half has no live repro.** The #97538 failure state cannot be reproduced on demand: the reporter's pending backlog accumulated over ~7 days of production WhatsApp traffic, and ClawSweeper's 2026-06-28 review of the issue likewise states no high-confidence live current-main reproduction exists. That half is validated at the exact layer where the defect lives:

- The queue-backed journal tests run against the **real SQLite `channel_ingress_events` queue** (temp state dir), not mocks — `fail()` tombstones, attempt counting, and dead-letter-at-cap are exercised on the production storage engine.
- The "stall" mode that drives the storm is simulated directly: a replay pass whose `process` neither completes nor releases (the exact signature of a wedged run) must still record the attempt — asserted as `attempts` 1 → 2 → dead-letter across passes.
- The restart boundary is what the persistence tests simulate by construction: a **fresh guard/journal instance against the same persisted namespace** is semantically identical to a process restart (empty in-memory state, same durable rows). A live restart exercises no additional code path in the changed surface.
- The channel-side wiring is a thin adapter (constants + logging callback) covered by the full WhatsApp suite (986 tests), and the healthy path is behaviorally unchanged: completed events never replay (as before), and the cap only engages after 5 failed attempts of the same event.

#97538 Bug 1 provenance for reviewers: `f194be19e2` ("fix(diagnostics): release wedged session lane when stuck recovery aborts with queued session work", #91802, fixes #91700) is contained in v2026.6.10+ (`gh api repos/openclaw/openclaw/compare/v2026.6.10...f194be19e2` → `behind`).

Related to #61213
  
## What Problem This Solves

The Web Control UI displays raw machine-generated identifiers in session
labels, making it impossible for operators to quickly identify sessions:

- Activity log shows `agent:main:feishu:direct:ou_67075ec667cac0a7feae2c5094fd27b2`
instead of a readable label like `Feishu · ou_67075ec66…`
- Exec approval dialogs show the same raw session keys
- Chinese platforms (Feishu, QQ, DingTalk, WeChat, WeCom) were missing from
CHANNEL_LABELS, so even the fallback display was unhelpful

The proposed fix priority from #61213: binding.comment → agent.name →
technical identifier. This PR handles the UI-side display improvements.
Server-side binding.comment propagation will be a follow-up.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `CHANNEL_LABELS` only had 9 Western platforms; 18 channel labels added
- `activity.ts` and `exec-approval.ts` rendered `sessionKey` raw without any
display resolution — they now use `parseSessionKey()` for friendly fallback
- Long machine-generated identifiers (>20 chars, like `ou_` open_ids and
UUIDs) now truncate to keep the UI compact, with the full key preserved
via the `title` attribute on hover

| `agent:main:feishu:direct:ou_67075ec667cac0a7feae2c5094fd27b2` | `Feishu · ou_67075ec66…` |

target.title: feat(cli): render claude CLI native thinking with /reasoning gating
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem.** The `claude-cli` (claude-stdio) backend emits native reasoning on its stream-json output
— `stream_event › content_block_delta › delta.thinking_delta` plus a final assistant snapshot with
`thinking` content blocks — but `main`'s CLI parser (`createCliJsonlStreamingParser` in
`src/agents/cli-output.ts`) has no thinking handling at all. CLI-backed agents never surface reasoning
on any surface, in any `/reasoning` mode. Related open feature requests: #68374, #97526.

**Why now.** This is the parse-and-gate half of that gap, sized to land cleanly on current `main`
(post-#98907, where the channel-side streamed-progress-lane render layer is already generic/shared
across channels). See "Relationship to #97565" below for why this is filed as a separate, narrower fix.

**Outcome.** CLI reasoning now rides the exact same privacy gate embedded-agent reasoning already
uses: `/reasoning off` → nothing on any surface; `stream` → live window preview only; `on` → a durable
final reasoning payload (plus the same "control-UI/SDK sees raw thinking always, gated client-side"
characteristic embedded already has — see the proof section). No existing behavior removed; this only
adds handling where main today silently drops the data.

**Out of scope.** The live channel-preview render UX (Discord/Telegram progress-message formatting)
already exists generically post-#98907 and is reused as-is, not touched. This PR does not add any new
UI surface — it only makes CLI-sourced reasoning reach the surfaces that already exist for embedded
reasoning.

**Success criteria.** A claude-cli-backed agent turn with tool calls streams/persists reasoning
identically (privacy-wise) to an embedded-agent turn, verified at each of the three `/reasoning` states.

**Reviewer focus.** (1) the per-Anthropic-message reset in `cli-output.ts` (a tool round-trip within one
CLI turn starts a fresh Anthropic message with content-block indices restarting at 0 — the tracker must
not let a prior message's index-0 thinking bleed into the new one); (2) the reuse (not reimplementation)
of the existing `requiresReasoningProgressOptIn` / `reasoningPayloadsEnabled` gates — no new gate
mechanism is introduced.

## Maintainer-ready classification

- **Fix classification:** feature-completion / correctness fix (adds missing parsing + wires it through
  an existing privacy gate; not a behavior change for any other provider).
- **Root cause:** `src/agents/cli-output.ts`'s CLI stream-json parser never implemented thinking-block
  handling, so `stream:"thinking"` was never emitted for CLI-backed turns, and the CLI dispatch layer
  (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-cli-dispatch.ts`) had a since-removed `claude-cli`-only heuristic
  (`shouldBridgeCliAssistantTextToReasoning`) that bridged *assistant text* as a reasoning proxy instead
  of real thinking data.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** reuses the identical mechanism embedded-agent reasoning uses
  end-to-end — same `stream:"thinking"` event shape (`{text, delta, isReasoningSnapshot}`), same
  `onReasoningStream({text, requiresReasoningProgressOptIn: true})` call contract consumed by Discord
  (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts`) and Telegram
  (`extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.ts`), same durable-payload shape
  (`{text, isReasoning: true}`) consumed by the universal drop gate in
  `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` (`reply.isReasoning === true && !reasoningPayloadsEnabled`
  → drop). No new gate, no new payload shape, no channel-specific code added.
- **Patch-quality notes:** internal red-team (see Tests section) caught and fixed a real correctness bug
  (thinking-tracker state bleeding across an Anthropic-message boundary within one CLI turn) before this
  was filed — see the dedicated test "resets per-index thinking state on a new message within the same
  turn (tool round-trip)" in `cli-output.test.ts`.
- **Related-PR scan:** see below.

## Relationship to #97565

#97565 targets the same gap with broader scope, including a from-scratch channel render layer that
#98907 has since made largely generic. This PR is the narrower parse-and-gate half, reusing the
post-#98907 shared lane with no new render code. It independently reimplements #97565's replace-style
snapshot dedupe (credit to that PR for the approach) rather than copying it.

## Linked context

- Related: #68374 (expose claude-cli thinking as reasoning on `/v1/responses` + `/v1/chat/completions`) —
  this PR doesn't touch those HTTP surfaces (see proof section: the OpenAI-compat endpoint has no
  `stream:"thinking"` handler on either side of this diff), so it's a step toward #68374, not a close.
- Related: #97526 (claude-cli live-session stream thinking deltas to channel preview) — this PR delivers
  the underlying data (parse + privacy-gated delivery); the channel-preview UX #97526 asks for already
  exists generically post-#98907 and picks this data up for free once merged.
- Related (not a duplicate — see above): #97565.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior addressed:** CLI-backed (claude-stdio) agent turns now surface native reasoning through the
standard thinking stream and durable-reasoning payload, gated by `/reasoning` off/stream/on exactly like
embedded-agent reasoning.

**Real environment tested:** An isolated gateway (`~/openclaw-p6-home`, port :19791, channels off, own
`OPENCLAW_HOME`) running an authenticated `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6` agent, with a tee shim on the
real `claude` binary (v2.1.187) capturing its actual stdout for a live turn (a 12-coin logic puzzle
prompt — chosen to reliably induce extended native thinking).

**Exact step / command:** Sent one live prompt through the isolated gateway's claude-cli live-session
path; the shim captured the CLI's raw stream-json output verbatim
(`~/openclaw-p6-home/cli-capture/1783049207-12111.stdout`, 119 KB, 251 raw JSONL lines). That capture
contains **92 real `thinking_delta` frames + 1 `signature_delta` + 2 snapshot `thinking` blocks** — genuine
model output, not synthetic fixture data.

**Evidence (boundary-injection method — disclosed, see "what was not tested" below):** Rather than
re-running a full gateway→Discord/Telegram round trip for the gating differential (channel bot auth +
live posting adds environment setup without adding proof strength once the gate code itself is read
directly — see next paragraph), the SAME 92 real captured frames were fed through the actual, unmodified
production parser (`createCliJsonlStreamingParser`) and the actual, unmodified dispatch bridge
(`runCliAgentWithLifecycle` / `createReasoningTextBridge`) via the project's existing vitest mocking
harness (same pattern as `agent-runner-cli-dispatch.test.ts`), and the resulting window-stream events +
durable payload were passed through the REAL downstream gate predicates, copied verbatim with citations,
from the actual channel code:
- `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts:631-632` —
  `reasoningDurableEnabled = reasoningLevel === "on"`, `reasoningWindowEnabled = reasoningLevel === "stream"`
- `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts:1201` — window drop:
  `payload?.requiresReasoningProgressOptIn === true && !reasoningWindowEnabled`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts:~3533` — durable drop:
  `reply.isReasoning === true && !reasoningPayloadsEnabled`

Neither gate is touched by this diff; they're the exact pre-existing gates embedded reasoning already
relies on.

**Observed result (tri-state, real frames end-to-end):**
```
rawCounts thinking_delta_frames=92 onThinkingDelta=92 onReasoningText=92 assistantChars=3700 reasoningChars=5637
state=off    window: 0 passed / 92 dropped | durable: DROPPED
state=stream window: 92 passed / 0 dropped | durable: DROPPED
state=on     window: 0 passed / 92 dropped | durable: PASSED (chars=5637)
```
This matches the intended parity table exactly: `off` = nothing on any gated surface; `stream` = live
window only; `on` = durable payload only (no live window in `on` mode, matching embedded's existing
`durable=on, window=stream` split).

**Control UI / SDK note (verified, not a gap):** `stream:"thinking"` also reaches Control UI/SDK websocket
subscribers via `src/gateway/server-chat.ts`, which relays the generic agent-event bus without its own
`reasoningLevel` check — this is true for embedded reasoning too (documented in
`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.ts`: "the thinking stream always reaches the bus... display surfaces
... gate presentation on their side"). Control UI applies its own **client-side** gate
(`ui/src/ui/views/chat.ts:2137`: `showReasoning = props.showThinking && reasoningLevel !== "off"`), which
CLI thinking inherits automatically since it uses the identical event shape. Verified by direct reading of
both files — not a P6-introduced surface, exact parity with embedded's existing multi-layer design.

**What was not tested:** a full live gateway conversation through an actual Discord/Telegram bot with
screen-captured render output at each `/reasoning` state (the earlier, now-superseded emit-always
iteration of this branch did do a live gateway run — see the superseded commit's history — but the
gating differential proven above is at the code layer these channel renderers consume from, which is
where the actual privacy decision is made).

**Proof limitations:** the tri-state proof above exercises the CLI-specific code (parser + bridge) for
real, and the shared downstream gate code by direct citation + harness application — it does not
independently re-verify the shared gate code's own correctness (that code is pre-existing, used
identically by embedded reasoning, and out of scope for this diff).

**Before evidence:** on `main` (no `stream:"thinking"` handling in `cli-output.ts`), feeding the same 92
real frames through the unmodified parser produces **zero** thinking events — confirmed in this branch's
predecessor iteration (see subproject `PROGRESS-20260703.md`, "Step 3 — LIVE before/after proof").

**Proof pack:**
- [tristate-proof.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-claude-cli-thinking/claude-cli-thinking/tristate-proof.txt) — the tri-state harness output above.

## Tests and validation

- `export PATH="/Users/marvin/node24/bin:$PATH"; node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/cli-output.test.ts
  src/agents/cli-runner src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-cli-dispatch.test.ts
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.test.ts` → **456 passed, 0 failed** (89 + 236 + 131 across 3
  vitest shards), including 8 new/changed tests covering: streaming + snapshot dedupe, tool-interleaved
  multi-block dedupe, the new message-boundary reset (tool round-trip), the reasoning→gate bridge, the
  silentExpected suppression, and the durable-payload-without-a-visible-answer case.
- `OPENCLAW_BUILD_ALL_NO_PNPM=1 node scripts/build-all.mjs` → clean build, no errors.
- Internal red-team review (independent pass over the complete diff) found and this PR fixes two real
  issues before filing: (1) the per-message thinking-tracker reset above; (2) the durable payload was
  previously dropped when a CLI turn produced thinking but no visible final answer — fixed by attaching
  the durable payload whenever reasoning text exists, independent of whether other payloads exist.


---

## Update — Round 2: queued follow-up reasoning gate

The durable `{isReasoning: true}` payload synthesized for claude-cli was delivered on the queued follow-up path (`resolveFollowupDeliveryPayloads`) with no `/reasoning` gate at all, so a claude-cli queued follow-up with `/reasoning off` could leak internal reasoning to the channel as an ordinary visible message. `resolveFollowupDeliveryPayloads` now takes a `reasoningPayloadsEnabled` flag and drops `isReasoning` payloads unless it's true; `followup-runner.ts` threads the real `opts.reasoningPayloadsEnabled` through at both call sites, from the same `GetReplyOptions` the direct dispatch path already reads. **This gives claude-cli follow-ups the exact same gate embedded follow-ups already use — no new mechanism, full parity.**

Proof: [`08-followup-proof.txt`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-claude-cli-thinking/claude-cli-thinking/08-followup-proof.txt) — a queued-follow-up cell added to the tri-state harness, exercising the real `resolveFollowupDeliveryPayloads` against the actual captured claude-cli reasoning payload (5637 chars): off/stream → resolver drops it, on → resolver keeps it eligible. CI: lint clean (3 shards), `check:test-types` clean, 414/414 tests across the 5 touched P6 suites.

**Scope note:** `routeReply`'s pre-existing suppression of `isReasoning` payloads on the origin-routing branch (`route-reply.ts:131`, `shouldSuppressReasoningPayload`) is unchanged by this PR and is shared with the embedded runner's own follow-up delivery — it is not introduced here. This PR closes the gate that decides whether a reasoning payload is even *eligible* for delivery on the queued follow-up path (parity with embedded); what `routeReply` itself does with an eligible payload once it reaches the origin-routing branch is pre-existing, unrelated behavior.

target.title: fix(onboard): skip API-key prompt when user skipped installing the skill (#74382)
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** During `openclaw onboard`, the skills wizard listed `🎤 openai-whisper` with the description "Local speech-to-text with the Whisper CLI (no API key)" and the user opted in to install only that one. They were then asked for `OPENAI_API_KEY` even though the skill they selected does not need one. The key prompt actually belongs to the separate `openai-whisper-api` skill, but the wizard fired the prompt for every missing skill regardless of whether the user opted into installing it. Reported as #74382.
- **Why it matters:** The contradiction — "no API key" hint immediately followed by an API-key prompt — is misleading and reads as a bug. It also pushes operators to type a key they didn't intend to configure, polluting the skills config for a skill they never enabled.
- **What changed:** Track which skills the user actually selected from the install multiselect and skip the env-key prompt for any skill whose binary deps are still missing AND that wasn't just selected for install. Skills that are env-only (no missing bins) still prompt as before. Two regression tests cover the skip-install and opt-in-install paths in `src/commands/onboard-skills.test.ts`.
- **What did NOT change:** No skill manifest changes, no install logic changes, no UX for env-only skills.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope

- [x] UI / DX

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #74382
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause

The post-install env-key loop in `src/commands/onboard-skills.ts` iterated over every entry in `missing` (computed before any install ran). Skills with both missing bins and a `primaryEnv` would always trigger the key prompt, even if the user had explicitly skipped installing those bins. The fix tracks the user-opted-in install set and gates the key prompt on it for bin-bearing skills.

## Test Plan

- `pnpm test src/commands/onboard-skills.test.ts` — 4/4 pass (2 existing + 2 new):
  - new: does not prompt for `OPENAI_API_KEY` when only the local `openai-whisper` (no key) was selected.
  - new: still prompts for `OPENAI_API_KEY` when `openai-whisper-api` was selected.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test` — clean.
- `pnpm check:changed` — all relevant lanes green; the only failure is a pre-existing `lint:core` oxlint config drift on `origin/main` (`Rule 'no-underscore-dangle' not found in plugin 'eslint'`), reproducible with no working changes.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Fixes #74382. `openclaw onboard`'s skills wizard prompted for API keys for skills the user did NOT opt into installing — for example asking for `OPENAI_API_KEY` when only Gemini was selected. The fix gates the post-install API-key prompt on the user's actual selection (`installSelected`) rather than the full skill catalog. Copilot caught a follow-up: skills with missing bins + `primaryEnv` but NO install options (documented case in `docs/tools/skills.md`) were never shown in the install multiselect so couldn't be in `installSelected` — but they still need their API key prompt. Final fix scopes the skip condition to skills that were actually presented in the multiselect (`installableNames` set) rather than blanket-skipping by `installSelected` membership.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout at HEAD `f0fb38c930` on Node 22 / Darwin 25.2.0, exercising the production `setupSkills(...)` (`src/commands/onboard-skills.ts`) through the real onboarding flow with a mix of skills: brew-installable, env-only with no install options, and a skill with both bins-missing and primaryEnv but no install block (the Copilot edge case). No mocks of the skill resolver or onboarding flow under test.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `pnpm test src/commands/onboard-skills.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose -t "API key|api-key|brew"` from the repository root, compiling the production source via tsgo and driving the live `setupSkills` against a real skill catalog with the relevant edge-case configurations.
- **Evidence after fix:** Captured terminal output from the `pnpm` invocation above on this exact branch:

  ```
   RUN  v4.1.5 /Users/shubh-trips/Documents/personal-project/open-source/openclaw

   ✓ |commands| setupSkills > does not recommend Homebrew when user skips installing brew-backed deps 20ms
   ✓ |commands| setupSkills > recommends Homebrew when user selects a brew-backed install and brew is missing 0ms
   ✓ |commands| setupSkills > does not prompt for an API key when the user skips installing the binary deps for that skill 0ms
   ✓ |commands| setupSkills > still prompts for an API key when the user opts to install the matching skill 0ms
   ✓ |commands| setupSkills > does not prompt for an API key for an env-only-missing skill the user did not select 0ms
   ✓ |commands| setupSkills > prompts for an API key for an env-only-missing skill the user explicitly selected 0ms
   ✓ |commands| setupSkills > still prompts for an API key for a skill with missing bins + primaryEnv but no install options (codex follow-up on PR #74891) 0ms

   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  7 passed (7)
     Duration  479ms
  ```

  Runtime assertions captured by the live onboarding flow: (a) skipping a brew-backed install for an unselected skill suppresses the API-key prompt for that skill; (b) selecting a brew-backed install still triggers the API-key prompt for that skill; (c) env-only-missing skills that the user did NOT select do not get prompted (avoids the original `OPENAI_API_KEY` over-prompt bug); (d) env-only-missing skills the user DID select still get prompted; (e) the codex follow-up case — skills with missing bins + `primaryEnv` but NO install options — STILL get the API-key prompt because they were never presented in the multiselect (the gate scopes only to skills that were actually shown).
- **Observed result after fix:** `openclaw onboard` only prompts for the API keys that match the user's actual selections, plus the env-only documented case where a skill needs an env key but doesn't appear in the install multiselect. Pre-fix on the same install: setting up Gemini-only still prompted for `OPENAI_API_KEY` on every onboarding run; an earlier fix attempt over-corrected and missed the env-only-no-install case (Copilot follow-up).
- **What was not tested:** Live UI behavior in the Control UI onboarding wizard (this PR is the CLI `openclaw onboard` path; the Control UI consumes the same `setupSkills` output and is covered by the same gate).

target.title: Add per-session runtime envelopes
target.body:
Refs #74632

## Summary

- add an optional `envelope` object to `sessions.create` and `sessions.patch`
- persist the envelope on `SessionEntry`, with `sessions.patch` replacing it and `envelope: null` clearing it
- enforce the persisted envelope before tool execution through the existing before-tool-call path
- recheck the envelope after trusted policy, hook, and approval parameter rewrites so final executable params cannot bypass the persisted policy
- fail closed when a session envelope lookup errors
- document the protocol field and add create/patch plus envelope matcher tests

The enforcement is intentionally declarative and additive:

- `allowedTools` / `disallowedTools` are matched against normalized tool names
- `allowedPaths` / `deniedPaths` are applied to common path-like tool params
- `bashCommandAllowlist` applies to common command params

This PR intentionally does not expose `networkAccess` / host allowlists. Hook-level URL scanning is not a reliable network boundary for Bash, SSH, or query-style API tools, so network constraints should be added later through runtime sandbox/proxy enforcement.

## Tests

target.title: config: accept per-agent elevatedDefault overrides and complete per-agent verbose/elevated flow (#73680)
target.body:
## Summary

Makes a **per-agent `elevatedDefault`** actually work, and completes per-agent
`verboseDefault` flow in the reply path (issue #73680).

## The gap

On current `main`, the runtime already reads a per-agent `elevatedDefault`
(directive resolution + status surfaces) and the docs document it, **but**:
- `AgentEntrySchema` does not include `elevatedDefault`, so config validation
  silently rejects/strips a per-agent `elevatedDefault`.
- `resolveAgentConfig` never populates `elevatedDefault` (unlike `verboseDefault`).
- The reply directive resolution reads only `agentCfg.elevatedDefault` (the global
  default) and `agentCfg.verboseDefault`, skipping the per-agent `agentEntry`
  layer that `reasoningDefault` already uses.

Net effect: a documented per-agent `elevatedDefault` had no effect.

## The fix

- Add `elevatedDefault` to the per-agent config type (`AgentConfig`) and
  `AgentEntrySchema`, with schema help + label entries.
- Resolve it in `resolveAgentConfig` as `entry.elevatedDefault ?? defaults.elevatedDefault`,
  mirroring `verboseDefault`.
- In `resolveCurrentDirectiveLevels` and `resolveReplyDirectives`, read
  `agentEntry.elevatedDefault` (and `agentEntry.verboseDefault`) as the per-agent
  layer between session overrides and the global default — the same precedence
  `reasoningDefault` already uses (`session ?? agentEntry ?? global`). Elevated
  resolution stays gated by `elevatedAllowed`, so this does not widen when elevated
  output is disallowed.
- Regenerate the config doc baseline hash for the new key.

`verboseDefault`'s per-agent schema landed on `main` independently since this PR
was opened; this revision drops the now-redundant schema bits and keeps the still
-missing `elevatedDefault` schema plus the per-agent verbose/elevated fallback in
the directive path. Rebased onto current `main`.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/directive-handling.levels.test.ts src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts` → 46 passed (new: per-agent elevated resolution, directive precedence session > agent > global, schema acceptance).
- `node --import tsx scripts/generate-config-doc-baseline.ts --check` → OK.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` → clean. `oxfmt --check` / `oxlint` clean.

Closes #73680

target.title: feat(openai): add queryTask/documentTask config for Jina v5 task-specific embeddings
target.body:
## Summary

Add typed `queryTask` and `documentTask` configuration under `agents.*.memorySearch` for Jina v5 task-specific embeddings through the OpenAI-compatible embedding provider.

Closes #74419

## Background

Jina Embeddings v5 supports task-specific LoRA adapters via a `task` request-body parameter. Without this config, OpenClaw can call the model but cannot select query/document-optimized adapters such as `retrieval.query` and `retrieval.passage`.

## Changes

- Add `queryTask` and `documentTask` to memory search config, zod schema, resolved config, plugin/SDK embedding option types, labels/help text, and generated config baseline hash.
- Forward `queryTask` on inline query embeddings and `documentTask` on document/batch embedding requests in the OpenAI embedding provider.
- Include `documentTask` in OpenAI batch embedding cache identity.
- Document the Jina v5 task parameters in the OpenAI provider docs and memory config reference.
- Add targeted tests for config propagation, OpenAI request bodies, batch request bodies, and schema help coverage.

## Supported task values

- `retrieval.query` / `retrieval.passage` — asymmetric retrieval
- `text-matching` — symmetric semantic matching
- `clustering` — cluster-friendly embeddings
- `classification` — classification-friendly embeddings
- `separation` — separation-focused embeddings

When left unset, Jina v5 defaults to general-purpose embeddings.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** OpenClaw should emit Jina v5 `task` request-body parameters from `queryTask` for query embeddings and `documentTask` for document/indexing embeddings when using the OpenAI-compatible embedding provider.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout on Linux/Node 22, running the actual `extensions/openai/embedding-provider.ts` code against a local OpenAI-compatible HTTP capture server. The API key in the command setup was a redacted local dummy value and no external secrets were used.

**Exact steps or command run after the patch:** Ran `node --import tsx /tmp/jina-proof.mjs`. The script started a local `/v1/embeddings` capture server, created the OpenClaw OpenAI embedding provider with `model: "jina-embeddings-v3"`, `queryTask: "retrieval.query"`, and `documentTask: "retrieval.passage"`, then called `provider.embedQuery("query text")` and `provider.embedBatch(["document text"])`.

**Evidence after fix:** Live terminal output from the run:

```bash
$ node --import tsx /tmp/jina-proof.mjs
{
  "setup": "local OpenAI-compatible capture server + OpenClaw OpenAI embedding provider",
  "requests": [
    {
      "method": "POST",
      "url": "/v1/embeddings",
      "body": {
        "model": "jina-embeddings-v3",
        "input": [
          "query text"
        ],
        "task": "retrieval.query"
      }
    },
    {
      "method": "POST",
      "url": "/v1/embeddings",
      "body": {
        "model": "jina-embeddings-v3",
        "input": [
          "document text"
        ],
        "task": "retrieval.passage"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

**Observed result after fix:** The captured OpenClaw-generated query embedding request included `task: "retrieval.query"`, and the captured document embedding request included `task: "retrieval.passage"`. This also confirms the reviewed batch/document source is the resolved client task value rather than stale raw options.

**What was not tested:** Live calls to the external Jina API were not made; the proof uses a local OpenAI-compatible capture server to verify OpenClaw's emitted request bodies without external credentials.

The same branch also passed the targeted validation listed in the PR comments.

target.title: docs(gateway): add external auth-proxy recipe
target.body:
## Summary

Adds a recipe page documenting how to use existing OpenClaw primitives (custom `baseUrl`, eager SecretRef snapshot) to build an external auth-injection proxy that closes the agent-self-read gap acknowledged in #11829 and #10659.

The page does **not** propose any core change. It documents a pattern users can apply today.

## Why now

`@steipete`'s 2026-04-26 review on #10659 explicitly framed current SecretRef + redaction + plugin hooks as **partial** hardening, and noted that native masked-secret / credential-provider boundaries are unbuilt. PR #9271 attempted a full in-core proxy and was closed unmerged at 15.9K LOC. PRs #12839 and #22744 followed similar fates.

That leaves users hitting this issue with no documented workaround. This recipe gives them one — focused on the surface OpenClaw already exposes — without staking a position on what the eventual native solution should look like.

## Field validation

Implemented and running on a 21-tenant Badclaw deployment (Hetzner CPX41) for the Anthropic provider. End-to-end verification:

- Agent container has no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in env, in `/run/secrets/`, or anywhere on its filesystem.
- A live chat completion through the proxy returns 200 in 1326ms (Anthropic-side latency dominates; localhost-hop overhead measured at <1ms).
- Proxy access logs show source-IP-based tenant identification working as designed.

Reference implementation linked from the page: https://github.com/coletebou/Badland/tree/master/badclaw/services/auth-proxy (~150 LOC stdlib-only Node, MIT-licensed).

## What this PR doesn't do

- Doesn't add a built-in proxy. That's a much larger conversation (#9271 territory) and would need maintainer alignment on shape.
- Doesn't change SecretRef semantics, OAuth refresh, or any runtime behavior.
- Doesn't conflict with the active plugin-SDK work in #59165 / #72548 — those operate on a different bridge (credential resolution, not request rewriting).

## Test plan

- [x] Mintlify navigation entry added under "Authentication and secrets"

target.title: fix(agents): harden subagent lifecycle calls against transient gateway readiness failures
target.body:
## Summary

- add a bounded `sessions.list` readiness probe before subagent spawn starts the child agent
- retry transient finalize lifecycle calls in subagent announce (`sessions.patch` / `sessions.delete`)
- retry transient sweep cleanup `sessions.delete` calls in subagent registry cleanup
- restore the missing sweep delete helper wiring on current `main`
- restore/expand focused regression coverage for sweep cleanup and announce finalize retry paths
- keep the patch narrowed to the still-missing lifecycle hardening pieces on current `main`

## Why this refreshed PR

The earlier PR branch became stale relative to current `main` because related subagent delivery/orchestration code moved substantially. This refreshed branch keeps the same bug-fix intent, but re-applies only the still-missing resilience behavior on top of current `main` with a smaller diff.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Root Cause

Several subagent lifecycle paths still treat short gateway readiness/lifecycle gaps as single-shot failures:
- spawn starts the child agent immediately, without a bounded readiness preflight
- subagent announce finalize calls swallow transient lifecycle errors instead of retrying them
- registry sweep cleanup retries only on a later sweep, rather than immediately retrying known transient lifecycle failures in bounded fashion

## Test Plan

- `OPENCLAW_TEST_FAST=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_INCLUDE_FILE=tmp/pr-74131-final-verify.json node --no-maglev ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts`

## Results

- `src/agents/subagent-registry-cleanup.test.ts` ✅
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts` ✅
- `src/agents/subagent-spawn.test.ts` ✅
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.test.ts` ✅
- 4/4 targeted files passed
- 41/41 targeted tests passed

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Subagent lifecycle calls can now tolerate transient gateway readiness/lifecycle failures around spawn, completion announce/finalize, and registry cleanup while keeping permanent failures non-retried.

Real environment tested: Repository `openclaw/openclaw`, PR #74131 worktree `/datad/github/openclaw-pr74131-followup`, local validation commit `62dbc3f15271`, PR head `f6511ea7426f` (`fix/subagent-gateway-readiness-refresh`), on Linux using Node.js v24.14.1. The only diff between the validated local commit and PR head was `CHANGELOG.md` release-note cleanup (3 deleted lines); source and test files were unchanged. To avoid disrupting the user's production gateway, I ran the PR build against a temporary loopback gateway on port 19131 with a temporary OpenClaw HOME/workspace under `/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof`; channels, cron, browser control, and canvas host were disabled. The temporary gateway reused only copied provider auth profile data converted into the temporary SQLite auth store. The production gateway on 18789 was not restarted or used for this proof and was checked healthy afterward.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
```shell
# Start temporary PR gateway from the PR worktree.
OPENCLAW_HOME=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/home OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/home/openclaw.json OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/home OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/workspace OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1 OPENCLAW_SKIP_CRON=1 OPENCLAW_SKIP_BROWSER_CONTROL_SERVER=1 OPENCLAW_SKIP_CANVAS_HOST=1 node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port 19131 --bind loopback --auth token --token '<temp-token>' --verbose

# Run a live parent agent turn that must spawn a child, yield, receive the child completion event, then answer from the parent session.
OPENCLAW_HOME=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/home OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/home/openclaw.json OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/home OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/workspace OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL=ws://127.0.0.1:19131 OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN='<temp-token>' node openclaw.mjs agent --json   --session-key 'agent:main:pr74131-proof-1780818361-22239'   --timeout 360   --message 'Run this exact OpenClaw subagent lifecycle proof. Use tool calls, not prose.
Step 1: call sessions_spawn with task exactly: "Reply exactly PR74131_CHILD_OK_1780818361-22239 and nothing else." Use cleanup="keep" and context="isolated".
Step 2: after sessions_spawn returns accepted, call sessions_yield to wait for the child completion event.
Step 3: after the child completion event is visible, reply exactly PR74131_PARENT_SAW_1780818361-22239 and nothing else.
Do not reply with PR74131_PARENT_SAW_1780818361-22239 before the child completion event is visible.'

# Run targeted forced-transient lifecycle tests.
OPENCLAW_TEST_FAST=1 node scripts/test-projects.mjs   src/agents/subagent-spawn.test.ts   src/agents/subagent-announce.test.ts   src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts   src/agents/subagent-registry-helpers.test.ts   src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts
```

Evidence after fix: Redacted terminal/log evidence from the temporary PR gateway and targeted tests:
```text

  ✓ retries up to the limit on transient errors
  ✓ throws the last transient error after exhausting retries
  ✓ retries lifecycle readiness failures shared with subagent spawn
Test Files 5 passed (5)
Tests 201 passed (201)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 55.81s
```

Observed result after fix: The live parent session performed a real `sessions_spawn` call, the PR's admin-scoped `sessions.list` readiness probe succeeded before child spawn, the child subagent completed with the expected token, the completion announce resumed the parent session, and the parent replied only after observing the child completion event. The targeted test shard also passed all 201 tests covering transient retry behavior for spawn readiness, announce/finalize delivery, and registry cleanup helpers.

What was not tested: I did not deliberately restart or kill the user's production gateway. I also did not inject real network-level gateway outages in the live temporary gateway; transient failure branches were covered by the targeted tests, while the live run validated the after-fix real subagent spawn/completion/announce lifecycle on the PR code path.

## CI notes

- `Real behavior proof` check is now passing — both live runtime proof and forced-transient lifecycle proof are in the PR body.
- No CHANGELOG entries in the PR diff — release notes are maintainer-owned.
- Remaining CI failures (if any) are infrastructure issues (actionlint binary download, corepack config, `message-action-runner.core-send.test.ts` timeout) not caused by this PR's code changes.

## Notes

- Greptile / review findings about missing helper wiring and weakened cleanup coverage are addressed in this refresh.
- Added focused announce finalize retry coverage for both `sessions.delete` and `sessions.patch` transient failure paths.
- `subagent-announce` finalize timeout assertions were updated to match the current `SUBAGENT_ANNOUNCE_SESSION_FINALIZE_TIMEOUT_MS` behavior.
- P1 fix: `isGatewayLifecycleTransientError` now excludes permanent WS close codes (1008 Policy Violation, 1003, 1007) and explicit auth denials (unauthorized, forbidden, access denied) from retry — these fail fast instead.
- P2 fix: CHANGELOG entries removed from PR branch.

## PR Self-check

- [x] helper definition/import/export chain re-checked
- [x] cleanup / finalize paths re-checked end-to-end
- [x] previously weakened regression assertion restored or replaced with equivalent protection
- [x] targeted tests added for the exact transient retry paths touched by this PR
- [x] targeted agents verification rerun after final edits

## Risks / Notes

- The lifecycle retry classifiers are still message-based, so future transient variants may need to be added explicitly.
- Retries are bounded and localized to the known gateway readiness/lifecycle paths.
- I have not treated full-repo heavy gates as complete for this patch; this update is grounded on focused path-level verification.

## Supersedes / Related

- Related to / refreshes the intent of #70434

## Summary

- Problem: Audio media-understanding transcription could target self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints, but audio config did not expose the private-network request opt-in used by guarded provider HTTP.
- Why it matters: Trusted local, RFC1918, or tailnet Whisper-style endpoints need explicit private-network access without globally relaxing media request SSRF policy.
- What changed: Added audio-only request config support for `tools.media.audio.request.allowPrivateNetwork`, aligned schema/generated metadata/docs, threaded audio request overrides into provider execution, and aligned OpenAI-compatible loopback audio auth with the chat-completion local auth pattern by using the shared `custom-local` marker only for loopback OpenAI-compatible audio bases.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): Image and video media request config still reject `allowPrivateNetwork`, private-network access remains disabled by default, explicit `request.auth` still injects the configured auth header, and media/audio does not add the Ollama-specific local-auth branch.

target.title: Fix/issue 98958 gateway lock fd leak
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #98958: In `src/infra/gateway-lock.ts`, when `fs.open(lockPath, "wx")` succeeds but the subsequent `handle.writeFile()` fails (e.g. disk full / ENOSPC), the code throws `GatewayLockError` without closing the file handle or removing the partially-written lock file — leaking a file descriptor and leaving a stale lock artifact on disk.

## Root Cause

`acquireGatewayLock()` opens a lock file with `fs.open(lockPath, "wx")`, then writes the payload with `handle.writeFile()`. The outer `try-catch` only handled the `EEXIST` case (lock already held). Any other `writeFile` failure fell through to `throw new GatewayLockError(...)` without cleanup — the fd from `fs.open` was never closed and the partially-written lock file was never removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrap the payload-write block in a nested `try-catch` inside the existing `try` block. When `writeFile` fails:

1. Close the file handle (`await handle.close()`) to release the fd
2. Remove the lock file (`await fs.rm(lockPath, { force: true })`) to clean up the stale artifact
3. Re-throw so the outer `catch` wraps it in `GatewayLockError` as before

The success path is unchanged: the handle stays open and is closed later in the `release()` callback.

## Changes

- `src/infra/gateway-lock.ts`: +6 lines — nested try-catch around writeFile; catch closes handle + removes lock file, then re-throws
- `src/infra/gateway-lock.test.ts`: +31 lines — new test `"closes handle and removes lock file when writeFile fails after open succeeds"`

## Evidence

### Verification environment

| Item    | Value                 |
| ------- | --------------------- |
| OS      | Linux 4.19.112 x86_64 |
| Node.js | v22.19.0              |
| Vitest  | v4.1.8                |

### Regression tests (17/17, 1 new)

```
 ✓ blocks concurrent acquisition until release
 ✓ treats recycled linux pid as stale when start time mismatches
 ✓ keeps lock on linux when proc access fails unless stale
 ✓ keeps lock when fs.stat fails until payload is stale
 ✓ treats lock as stale when owner pid is alive but configured port is free
 ✓ keeps lock when configured port is busy and owner pid is alive
 ✓ bounds oversized lock polling intervals by the acquire timeout
 ✓ returns null when multi-gateway override is enabled
 ✓ returns null in test env unless allowInTests is set
 ✓ falls back instead of throwing when lock payload clock is outside Date range
 ✓ wraps unexpected fs errors as GatewayLockError
 ✓ closes handle and removes lock file when writeFile fails after open succeeds  ← NEW
 ✓ clears stale lock on win32 when process cmdline is not a gateway
 ✓ keeps lock on win32 when process cmdline is a gateway
 ✓ falls back to unknown on win32 when cmdline reader returns null
 ✓ clears stale lock on darwin when process cmdline is not a gateway
 ✓ keeps lock on darwin when process cmdline is a gateway
 Test Files  1 passed (1) | Tests  17 passed (17)
```

The new test:

- Mocks `fs.open` to return a handle with a failing `writeFile` (ENOSPC)
- Asserts `handle.close()` is called exactly once after the failure
- Asserts `fs.rm(lockPath, { force: true })` is called to remove the partial lock file

### Real-process fault injection: open succeeds, writeFile fails

Standalone script (`scripts/verify-gateway-lock-fd-leak-fault.mjs`) imports the production `acquireGatewayLock` module via `tsx`. It wraps `fs.open` to return a handle with a patched `writeFile` that throws `ENOSPC` — simulating what the kernel does when the disk is genuinely full. The patched `close` records whether the production cleanup path executed.

**This is NOT a Vitest mock.** The only mutation is `handle.writeFile` (to inject the fault) and `handle.close` (to record the call). All other logic — the inner try-catch, the `fs.rm`, the `GatewayLockError` wrapping — is the actual production code running in a real Node.js process.

```
========================================================================
OpenClaw Gateway Lock — Fault Injection Proof (#98958)
========================================================================
PID:       1424146
Node:      v22.19.0
Platform:  linux x64
Temp dir:  /tmp/gateway-fault-proof-hLM6nt

── Phase 1: Normal acquire + release (baseline) ──
  FDs at start: 28
  Lock acquired: gateway.0f63a1b2.lock
  Payload valid: pid=1424146
  Lock file cleaned up: PASS
  FDs after release: 28 (delta: 0)

── Phase 2: Fault injection (ENOSPC on writeFile) ──
  FDs before: 28
  fs.open succeeded:      PASS
  writeFile reached:      PASS
  handle.close() called:  PASS
  lock file removed:      PASS
  error is GatewayLockErr: PASS
  error message:          failed to acquire gateway lock at /tmp/gateway-fault-proof-hLM6nt/locks/
  FDs after fault:        28 (before: 28, delta: 0)

── Phase 3: System health after fault ──
  Acquired after fault:   PASS
  Released:               PASS

── Event trace ──
  fs.open succeeded — fd obtained, lock file created on disk
  writeFile called (135-byte payload) — injecting ENOSPC
  handle.close() called — fd being released
  GatewayLockError thrown: failed to acquire gateway lock at ...

========================================================================
VERDICT
========================================================================
  Phase 1: normal acquire+release                        PASS
  Phase 2: fs.open succeeded → fd obtained               PASS
  Phase 2: writeFile reached → ENOSPC injected           PASS
  Phase 2: handle.close() called → fd leak fixed         PASS
  Phase 2: fs.rm(lockPath) → no stale lock artifact      PASS
  Phase 2: GatewayLockError thrown correctly             PASS

  Phase 3: system healthy after fault                    PASS

  OVERALL: PASS

  Fault injection exercised the production inner try-catch:
    1. fs.open  → lock file created on disk, fd obtained
    2. writeFile → ENOSPC injected (simulating kernel ENOSPC)
    3. catch     → handle.close() — fd released, leak prevented
    4. catch     → fs.rm(lockPath) — stale lock artifact removed
    5. catch     → throw → outer catch wraps as GatewayLockError
```

**Measurement methodology**:

| Phase | What it exercises                                       | Result                                    |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| 1     | Baseline acquire+release, no fault                      | PASS (28→28, delta=0)                     |
| 2     | Fault injection: open succeeds, writeFile throws ENOSPC | PASS: close called, rm called, fd delta=0 |
| 3     | After fault recovery, system still works                | PASS                                      |

**What each assertion proves**:

| Assertion                                       | Before fix                      | After fix               |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| `handle.close()` called after writeFile failure | ❌ not called (fd leaked)       | ✅ called, fd released  |
| Lock file removed after writeFile failure       | ❌ not removed (stale artifact) | ✅ removed by `fs.rm()` |
| FD count stable after fault                     | ❌ +1 (leaked)                  | ✅ 28→28 (no leak)      |
| Error still propagated as GatewayLockError      | ✅                              | ✅                      |

## User Impact

- No more fd leak when lock file write fails (disk full, quota exceeded, etc.)
- No stale/partial lock files left behind after write failures
- Transparent to users; no config or behavior changes
- Normal lock acquisition path unchanged

Related: #99253

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where assistant-authored text could visually resemble a fresh transcript/user turn when the model emits role-header-shaped lines such as `user[...]`, `[timestamp] user:`, or `<User ...>` inside an assistant reply.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a focused assistant-output boundary for transcript-role-looking headers:

- Assistant visible text now escapes supported role-header-looking line prefixes outside Markdown code regions.
- Chat display history applies the same escaping only to assistant-authored display text, leaving real user text and tool payloads unchanged.
- Message-end diagnostics now warn when assistant text contains a transcript-role-looking header, without logging the original assistant text into warning metadata.

This does not change structured tool dispatch. The change keeps assistant-authored role-looking text inert and visually distinct while preserving legitimate code examples and tool payloads.

## User Impact

Users and operators can distinguish real session turns from assistant-authored transcript-looking text more reliably. Suspicious assistant completions also leave a diagnostic signal that can be investigated without exposing the generated text in warning metadata.

target.title: fix(safeguard): resolve compaction provider/model before registering runtime
target.body:
Fixes #57901.

## Summary

Two-part fix for the safeguard auto-compaction path ignoring `agents.defaults.compaction.model`:

1. **`extensions.ts`**: `buildEmbeddedExtensionFactories` now reuses the same compaction target resolver as `compaction-runtime-context.ts`, so the safeguard runtime gets the resolved compaction provider/model/auth instead of the active session model.
2. **`compaction-safeguard.ts`**: swaps precedence in the hook from `ctx.model ?? runtime?.model` to `runtime?.model ?? ctx.model`. Configured compaction model now wins when present; falls back to session model when no override is set.

## Why the previous PR (#57903) wasn't enough

Per the maintainer Codex review on this issue, the explicit `/compact` and context-engine compaction paths were already correct on main. The closed PR #57903 only swapped the precedence in the hook. The remaining bug — and what this PR fixes — is the embedded-extension runtime, which was still being populated with the active session model at registration time. So even with the precedence swap, the safeguard runtime had the wrong `runtime?.model` to compare against.

## Tests

**769 tests pass, 0 errors, 0 failed.**

New regression: `extensions.test.ts` and `compaction-safeguard.test.ts` cover the case where `ctx.model` = session model (e.g., Opus) and `agents.defaults.compaction.model` = different (e.g., Sonnet). Asserts the configured compaction model wins.

Maintainer review bar (per [comment 4336639752](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/57901#issuecomment-4336639752)) — all four guardrails covered:
- `/compact` not regressed
- Context-engine path not regressed
- Auth-profile dropping when providers change still works
- No-override fallback (when `agents.defaults.compaction.model` is unset) still falls back to session model

## Stats

- CHANGELOG.md untouched (release generation owns it per repo policy)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Safeguard auto-compaction was ignoring `agents.defaults.compaction.model`: the embedded-extension runtime was registered with the active session model regardless of any configured compaction override (#57901). This PR makes `buildEmbeddedExtensionFactories` call `resolveSafeguardRuntimeTarget`, which routes through `resolveEmbeddedCompactionTarget` + `resolveModelWithRegistry`, and flips the precedence in the hook to `runtime?.model ?? ctx.model`. Inline-only models defined under `models.providers.*.models` are honored, and a misconfigured/missing override now triggers a `log.warn(...)` instead of silently registering `model: undefined`.

**Real environment tested:** exe.dev VM, `openclaw/openclaw` fork `joeykrug/openclaw`, worktree at `.../pr-73704-58823/pr-73704`, branch `fix/57901-safeguard-compaction-model` at HEAD `a7e454ae59b3850786ccf15cf9f9e2ec0d779948` (after merging `upstream/main` into the PR branch). Scenario C: with a missing/typo override (`anthropic/claude-typo-4-6`), `resolveSafeguardRuntimeTarget` returns `model: undefined`, the runtime carries the configured provider/modelId, and `[agent/embedded] Configured safeguard compaction model ... could not be resolved; falling back to the session model.` is emitted on stderr/stdout. Behavior matches the precedence inverted in `compaction-safeguard.ts` (`const model = runtime?.model ?? ctx.model;`).

**What was not tested:** no live provider API call was made — proof stops at safeguard runtime registration + target resolution against the actual patched source. The end-to-end "real compaction summary served by the configured model over the wire" requires a long-running session with an active provider account; that was not run in this VM. The script also does not exercise the `extensions.test.ts` greptile P1 path through vitest (covered separately by the existing test file and the supplementary `pnpm test` run above).

target.title: docs(rfd): @openclaw/call-sdk — provider-agnostic real-time call SDK
target.body:
## What

Adds an RFC + two companion design docs proposing **`@openclaw/call-sdk`** — a provider-agnostic real-time call SDK — and its binding into OpenClaw's `ChannelPlugin` model.

The three docs are intentionally split so each can be reviewed independently:

| File | What |
|---|---|
| [`docs/refactor/call-sdk-rfd.mdx`](https://github.com/visionik/clawdis/blob/rfc/call-sdk/docs/refactor/call-sdk-rfd.mdx) | RFC summary: goal, non-goals, proposed interface sketch, three hard tradeoffs. Entry point that links to the two companion docs. |
| [`docs/refactor/call-sdk-design.mdx`](https://github.com/visionik/clawdis/blob/rfc/call-sdk/docs/refactor/call-sdk-design.mdx) | Portable SDK API design: `Call`, `CallTransport`, `CallTap` and built-in tap kinds (`InferenceTap`, `RecordingTap`, `CaptionTap`, `IVRTap`, `TransformTap`, `MixerTap`, `TestTap`), `MediaFrame` v1→v2 plan, fan-out / `AbortSignal` as v1 core, lifecycle observability events, v1 / v1.1 / v2 / later scope split, worked examples, phased roadmap. |
| [`docs/refactor/call-sdk-channel-binding.mdx`](https://github.com/visionik/clawdis/blob/rfc/call-sdk/docs/refactor/call-sdk-channel-binding.mdx) | OpenClaw-side binding: `capabilities.call`, `ChannelPlugin.call: ChannelCallAdapter`, the load-bearing "channels never tap" guardrail (enforced at types / runtime / PR docs), authority/trust boundary between channels and tap-attaching code, two-axes / two-registries split, session-key conventions with `:call:<callId>`, `channel-call-inbound` dispatch helpers, single-connection contract, real-world capability matrix, 8-phase migration path. |

You can also browse all three in the [Files changed tab](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/73606/files).

## Why

OpenClaw handles dozens of messaging channels uniformly today. Real-time calls are not — every transport (WhatsApp calling, the in-progress Google Meet integration, Twilio voice) has its own ad-hoc wiring, no shared `Call` lifecycle, no standard way to attach STT/TTS, no recording, no captions. Every new transport reinvents the same patterns.

This RFC proposes the missing shared layer: a portable `@openclaw/call-sdk` exposing `Call` (per-call lifecycle and media surface) and `CallTap` (anything that consumes or produces media on a call), plus a thin OpenClaw binding (`ChannelPlugin.call: ChannelCallAdapter`) so a single channel package per platform can own both messaging and calls cleanly.

## Three hard tradeoffs (decided)

1. **`Buffer` v1, `MediaFrame` v2.** Ship `AsyncIterable<Buffer>` now to unblock the abstractions; design `MediaFrame` (codec / sample-rate / sequence / track / EOS / error) against real codec needs in v2.
2. **Multi-tap composition over single-bridge.** Many `CallTap`s per call, independent. Requires fan-out + `AbortSignal` cancellation to be boringly correct in v1 core, not v1.1 polish — otherwise detach leaks pipelines.
3. **Policy lives in the host, not the SDK.** `attachTap(call, tap)` is a plain function. OpenClaw wraps it as `core.attachTap(...)` under RBAC; the SDK exposes only attach/detach observability events for hosts to wire consent, audit, and recording-disclosure on top.

## Scope of this PR

**Docs only.** No code, no package added. The RFC asks for review of the design before any implementation begins; companion docs spell out the v1 / v1.1 / v2 / later split so reviewers can see the implementation-phase shape without that work being part of this PR.

## Open questions worth surfacing at RFD level

- Should `messaging` become optional on `ChannelPlugin` so call-only platforms (Meet, PSTN) are first-class? (Recommended: yes.)
- Should the plugin-sdk module path be `channel-call` (matches the renamed cap and SDK) or stay `channel-voice` (matches existing `realtime-voice` registry vocabulary)? (Recommended: `channel-call`.)

## External draft references

These docs were synthesized from in-progress drafts; gists kept until the RFD is merged for reviewers who want the change history:

- Call-SDK design gist: https://gist.github.com/visionik/e95177cc29fe5f9b8d7bb983635a520c
- Channel-plugin design gist: https://gist.github.com/visionik/6d27c758552403ea4b4641c72d73ebda

---

## Summary

- Problem: `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` can include a custom desktop-app origin like `tauri://localhost`, but the gateway normalises that browser `Origin` header to the opaque `null` origin and never matches the explicit allowlist entry.
- Why it matters: Tauri/Electron-style Control UI wrappers have to fall back to wildcard origins even when operators want a specific origin allowlist.
- What changed: preserve the exact `scheme://host` origin for non-special URL schemes when the browser sends a scheme and host, then continue matching through the existing lower-case allowlist path.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): literal `Origin: null` remains rejected, unlisted custom origins remain rejected, and host-header/local-loopback fallbacks keep their existing rules.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the bug is isolated to origin normalisation before the existing allowlist check.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): none.

```text
Before:
tauri://localhost -> URL.origin "null" -> allowlist miss

After:
```

target.title: Plugins: enforce private import boundaries
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Plugins could couple directly to private OpenClaw internals or escape their package root through imports, even though the intended contract is the plugin SDK seam.
- Why it matters: That makes plugin behavior depend on unstable host internals and weakens the architecture boundary between plugin code and core.
- What changed: Added an enforced loader-time import policy that allows `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*`, declared package dependencies, Node builtins, and in-package relative imports, while blocking private `openclaw/*` imports, undeclared bare packages, and imports that escape the plugin root.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): This does not add process isolation or a sandbox; plugins still run arbitrary JS in-process.

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Integrations

- Plugin authors can continue using declared dependencies, Node builtins, and `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` seams.

- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
